We've had our Slack integration running for a few months alongside Salesforce, Okta, and Jira, and it's mostly been reliable for routing billing alerts to our #ops channel. Last week we onboarded a new team and tried to add a second Slack channel for API error alerts specifically, following the setup docs step by step.

Here's what we're getting when we try to add the second channel destination:

```
Error: channel_binding_conflict
At: /integrations/slack/channels POST
Detail: workspace already has 1 active binding for alert_type=api_error
Status: 409
```

Is multi-channel routing for the same alert type just not supported yet? If so, I'd like to put in a request for it since we manage several regional teams that each want their own channel for the same alert category.
answer: You're right — currently each alert type can only bind to one Slack channel per workspace, which is why you're hitting the channel_binding_conflict error when adding a second destination for api_error alerts. This is a common request, so I'm logging it as a feature request for multi-channel routing per alert type and attaching your use case with regional teams; in the meantime, a workaround some customers use is a Slack workflow that re-broadcasts from the single bound channel to others.

subject: Audit log export and retention settings
body: I'm setting up our compliance review process for Granite Foods and need to export audit logs going back 90 days from the Admin Console. Right now I can only see the last 30 days in the UI, and there's no obvious export button. Could you point me to documentation on log retention settings and whether we can extend the window, plus how to add specific IP ranges to an allowlist for console access?
answer: Thanks for reaching out. Audit log retention on the Starter plan is capped at 30 days in the UI, but we can generate a one-time CSV export covering up to 90 days on request while you evaluate whether an upgrade is needed for ongoing extended retention. I'll also send over our documentation link covering allowlist configuration for console access, and follow up within one business day with the export file.

subject: Multiple failed card charges on our account
body: We've had three consecutive failed payment attempts on our Willow Capital account this week, on the 4th, 6th, and 8th, and I just got a notice that our seats may be suspended soon. The card on file hasn't expired and has plenty of available credit, so I'm not sure why the charges are being declined. Can someone check the payment gateway logs and let us know if this is on our end or Northwind's?
answer: I'm sorry for the trouble this is causing. I've pulled up the transaction records and can see the three declined attempts you mentioned; the decline codes point to a bank-side flag rather than a Northwind processing issue, but I'm escalating to our payments team to confirm before your next billing cycle. In the meantime I've paused any automatic seat suspension for 5 business days so this doesn't disrupt your team while we sort out the card issue.

subject: Scheduled syncs failing since this morning
body: Our nightly data pipeline sync from the ERP connector to the warehouse has failed for the past two runs, at 2:00 AM and 2:00 AM again today. The dashboard shows status 'Failed' with error code SYNC_TIMEOUT_504 and latency spiking to over 40 seconds per batch before the job drops. This is affecting financial close numbers for over 160 users who rely on these reports being current by 8 AM.
answer: Thank you for flagging this immediately, I understand the impact on your financial close process. We're seeing elevated latency on the ERP connector cluster and are actively investigating the SYNC_TIMEOUT_504 errors; I've triggered a manual retry on both failed batches and will monitor closely. I'll update you within the hour with root cause and an ETA for the next scheduled sync to complete successfully.

subject: Seat count discrepancy causing billing error
body: I'm reviewing our latest invoice for Harbor Energy and it lists 7 active seats, but we only have 4 employees using Northwind Cloud. This has bumped us into a higher billing tier unexpectedly and I need this corrected before the next charge goes through. Can you confirm our actual active seat count and adjust the invoice accordingly?
answer: Thanks for catching this before the charge processed. I've reviewed your account and confirmed only 4 seats show recent login activity; it looks like 3 deactivated user accounts were still counted toward your billing tier due to a sync delay. I'm correcting the seat count now and will issue a revised invoice reflecting the accurate tier within the next few hours.

subject: Pagination broken on /v2/events endpoint
body: Since yesterday our integration pulling events via the /v2/events endpoint has been returning duplicate records across pages instead of advancing the cursor correctly. We rely on this for near-real-time operations reporting and right now we're seeing the same 500 records repeat on every page request instead of moving forward. Is this related to the pagination changes mentioned in the recent API changelog?
answer: Thank you for the detailed report, this matches an issue we're currently investigating tied to a recent update on cursor handling for /v2/events. Our API team has identified the regression and is preparing a fix; in the meantime, I'd recommend temporarily switching to offset-based pagination as a workaround, and I'll send documentation on that approach along with an update as soon as the cursor fix is deployed.

subject: Deactivated users still showing as active
body: We deactivated 12 users from the Admin Console last week after a reorg at Blue Analytics, but they still appear as active in the audit log and are still consuming licensed seats according to our latest usage report. This is causing confusion for our access reviews and we need this fixed quickly since it affects compliance reporting due this Friday. Can you confirm whether this is a display bug or something more serious?
answer: This has been escalated to our engineering team as a priority bug, as deactivated accounts should immediately reflect in both the audit log and seat count. We've confirmed a sync delay affecting a subset of accounts deactivated in the past week, including the 12 you mentioned, and are pushing a fix now. I'll confirm once your audit log and seat usage are corrected, well ahead of your Friday deadline.

subject: Transform step failing on connector pipeline
body: We're seeing repeated failures in the transform stage of our logistics data pipeline for Granite Robotics, specifically on the field-mapping step after the connector pulls from our warehouse management system. The error shown is 'TRANSFORM_ERR: null reference at row batch 214' and it's happening on roughly 1 in 5 runs, with no clear pattern tied to data volume. Latency on successful runs has also crept up over the last week.
answer: Thanks for the detailed report and the specific error reference, that's very helpful. The null reference at the transform step suggests a schema mismatch that's intermittently present in incoming batches from the WMS connector; we're pulling logs for the failed runs now to identify which field is triggering it. I'll follow up with findings and a recommended fix for the mapping configuration, and will also look into the latency increase you noticed.

subject: Biometric login crashing mobile app
body: Several staff at Atlas Academy have reported the mobile app crashing immediately after attempting Face ID login on iOS, starting with the latest app update two days ago. The app opens, shows the login screen, and closes as soon as biometric authentication is triggered, forcing users to fall back to password login every time. This is happening across multiple iOS devices, not just one person's phone.
answer: Thank you for reporting this with the timing details, that helps narrow it down to the recent release. We've reproduced a crash tied to biometric authentication handling in the latest iOS build and our mobile team is treating it as a priority fix. In the meantime, password login should continue to work as a stable fallback, and I'll update you as soon as the patched build is available.

subject: Offline mode crashes when reconnecting
body: Our field teams at Willow Analytics use the mobile app extensively in offline mode, and we're seeing consistent crashes when connectivity is restored and the app attempts to sync queued actions. This has been happening for about a week across a large number of devices, and any push notifications queued during the offline period seem to never arrive after the crash. Given our team size, this is affecting a significant number of daily users.
answer: Thank you for flagging this, especially given the scale of impact across your field teams. We've identified an issue in the offline sync reconnection logic that appears to be causing the crash and dropping queued push notifications in the process; our mobile engineering team is actively working on a fix. I'll keep you updated on progress and will let you know as soon as a patched version is ready for rollout.

subject: Duplicate alert notifications going out repeatedly
body: We've noticed that our alerting rules in Northwind Notifications are sending the same alert multiple times, sometimes 3 or 4 duplicate emails for a single triggered event, over the past several days. This is causing confusion among our legal team who think there are separate incidents when it's actually one. Can you help identify why deduplication isn't working as expected for our alert rules?
answer: Thank you for the clear description, duplicate alerts like this usually point to a deduplication window misconfiguration or a retry loop on the delivery side, and we want to get this resolved quickly given the confusion it's causing your team. I'm pulling the delivery logs for your alert rules now to identify which notifications are triggering duplicates and will follow up with findings and a fix, or a configuration adjustment if needed.

subject: Mobile app crashes immediately on launch after latest update
body:
Since updating to the latest version of the Northwind mobile app this morning, our field staff can't get past the splash screen. The app crashes within 1-2 seconds of opening on both iOS and Android devices. We've had at least 14 of our 22 users report this so far, and it's blocking check-ins for our travel groups currently on-site.

We tried clearing app cache and reinstalling on two devices with no change. Push notifications still seem to arrive even though the app won't open, which is odd.
answer: Thanks for the detailed report and the device count, that helps us gauge scope quickly. We're seeing a crash pattern tied to the last release affecting login-state restoration on cold start, and our mobile team is actively working a fix. In the meantime, could you have affected users try logging out via the web portal to clear their session token, then reinstalling — this has resolved the crash for a few other customers while we finalize the patch.

subject: Question about storage retention settings for archived uploads
body:
We're reviewing our data retention policy and I want to confirm how Northwind Storage handles files after they hit the retention limit we configured (currently 365 days). Are files automatically purged, or do they move to a cold tier we can still restore from? We have roughly 40TB uploaded across our regional offices and want to make sure nothing is deleted before we've had a chance to review it.

Also, is there a way to get a report of what's approaching its retention expiry date, ideally per upload bucket?
answer: Good question, and glad you're checking before relying on defaults. Files that hit the retention limit are moved to a 30-day soft-delete state before permanent purge, so you'd have a window to restore anything flagged incorrectly. For visibility, you can enable the retention expiry report under Storage > Settings > Retention Reports, which lists items nearing expiry per bucket and can be scheduled weekly via email.

subject: Seat upgrade charged wrong amount and invoice doesn't match
body:
We upgraded from 100 to 128 seats on our Pro plan last week, and the invoice we received (INV-88213) charged us for a full month at the new seat count instead of prorating from the upgrade date of the 14th. This is a $612 discrepancy. Our finance team flagged it and is asking for a corrected invoice or refund before end of month close.

Can someone confirm how proration is supposed to work here and issue the adjustment?
answer: Thank you for flagging this with the invoice number, that lets us look directly at the transaction. Seat upgrades should prorate from the effective date, so a full-month charge on the new count is not expected behavior — this looks like a billing calculation error on our end. I'm escalating this to our billing team now to issue a corrected invoice with the proration applied, and I'll follow up within one business day with the adjustment amount.

subject: Request to route duplicate alerts to different email groups
body:
We use Northwind Notifications to send billing and system alerts to our ops team, but right now every alert type goes to the same shared inbox, causing a lot of noise and duplicate tickets being opened internally. We'd like to set up routing so that billing alerts go to our finance distribution list and system/API alerts go to our engineering list instead.

Is this kind of rule-based routing supported today, or is it on the roadmap? We have 293 seats and this affects most of our regional managers who get flooded daily.
answer: Thanks for the clear use case — routing by alert category is something we can help with. Currently you can create routing rules under Notifications > Routing Rules, filtering by alert type or source tag and directing them to specific email groups; this should let you separate billing from system/API alerts without custom development. I'll walk through setting up two rules for you and confirm they're working as expected within a day.

subject: Dashboards extremely slow, blocking month-end reporting
body:
Our dashboards have been taking 30-60 seconds to load charts since yesterday afternoon, and some panels time out entirely with a blank chart area. This is happening for all 16 of our users, not just me, and it's actively blocking our month-end financial reporting which is due today.

We haven't changed anything on our end recently — no new data sources or shared dashboards added this week. Can someone look into this urgently?
answer: I understand the urgency given your reporting deadline, and I'm escalating this immediately as a priority incident. We're seeing elevated query latency on the dashboard rendering service that started yesterday and our engineering team is actively investigating; I'll update you within the hour with either a fix or a workaround such as exporting raw data directly while charts recover. Thank you for your patience while we get this resolved.

subject: Recurring card failures blocking our monthly billing
body:
Our company card has been declined three times this week when Northwind tried to process our Starter plan renewal, even though the card is active and has sufficient funds. We got error emails referencing 'card_declined - do_not_honor' each time. This is now affecting our 22 seat licenses which show as past due, and I'm worried access will be suspended.

We've confirmed with our bank there's no block on their end. Can you check what's happening on Northwind's side and help us get this resolved before seats get locked?
answer: I'm sorry for the disruption this is causing, and I want to get this fixed before it affects your team's access. The 'do_not_honor' response usually comes from the issuing bank flagging the transaction pattern rather than an account issue on our side, but I'm pulling the transaction logs now to confirm nothing looks off with how we're submitting the charge. In the meantime, I'm placing a temporary hold on any seat suspension for your account while we sort this out, and I'll follow up shortly with either a resolution or an alternate payment method suggestion.

subject: Urgent: need to restore storage backup after failed migration
body:
We ran a migration script against our Storage buckets last night as part of a compliance audit prep, and it looks like it overwrote roughly 8,200 files in the 'client-records-2023' bucket with empty placeholders. We need to restore from the backup snapshot taken before the migration started, which should be from approximately 11:40 PM UTC on the 6th.

This is time-sensitive as our compliance team needs these records available for an audit review tomorrow morning. Please advise on restore process and expected timeline.
answer: This has been escalated to our security and compliance response team given the audit deadline and data impact. We do have a snapshot retained from 11:40 PM UTC on the 6th, and we're initiating a restore of the 'client-records-2023' bucket now — this typically takes under an hour for a dataset of this size, and I'll confirm completion and file counts as soon as it finishes. We'll also provide a summary log of the restore for your compliance documentation.

subject: Need to change dashboard export settings
body:
Our team has been using Northwind Dashboards heavily this quarter to track store performance across our retail locations, and we've built out about 40 shared dashboards used by regional managers. Everything was fine until last week when we started noticing exports taking much longer than usual.

The actual issue is that CSV exports from dashboards with more than 3 charts now time out after about 2 minutes with a generic 'export failed' message, whereas before they completed in under 30 seconds. This is blocking our regional managers from getting weekly reports out on time.
answer: Thanks for the detailed history — that helps confirm this is a regression rather than an existing limitation. Export timeouts on multi-chart dashboards match a known issue introduced in a recent update to the export renderer, and our team is working on a fix. As a workaround in the meantime, exporting charts individually or splitting dashboards into smaller sets should avoid the timeout, and I'll update this ticket once the underlying fix is deployed.

subject: Restore from backup taking unusually long, need status
body:
We initiated a restore from backup on one of our Storage buckets ('legal-archive-2022') three days ago after an accidental bulk delete affected around 1,900 files. The restore job still shows 'in progress' with no percentage or ETA in the admin console. Support ticket reference from initial delete incident was submitted separately last week.

Could someone check the actual status of this restore job and let us know if it's stuck or just slow? We'd like to close out our internal incident report once this completes.
answer: Thanks for checking in on this — a restore sitting in 'in progress' for three days without a visible ETA is longer than typical for a bucket of that size, so I'm looking into the job status directly on our end now. I'll confirm whether it's actively processing or stalled, and if needed we can manually re-trigger the restore. I'll have an update for you within a few hours so you can close out your internal incident report.

subject: Webhook deliveries failing intermittently with 429 responses
body:
We're seeing intermittent webhook delivery failures on our API Platform integration over the past two days, with our endpoint logs showing repeated 429 rate_limit_exceeded responses from Northwind even though our traffic volume hasn't changed. This is affecting order-status webhooks for our energy monitoring integration, roughly 200-300 failed deliveries per day out of an estimated 15,000.

We also noticed the webhook retry backoff seems to have changed recently — retries now happen much faster than before, which may be compounding the rate limit issue. Can you confirm if there was a recent change to webhook rate limits or retry behavior, and if there's an SDK update we should apply?
answer: Thanks for the specifics on volume and timing — that's helpful for tracing this. There was a recent adjustment to webhook retry backoff intervals as part of a platform update, and it's possible this is causing bursts that trip rate limits sooner than before; I'm escalating to our platform team to confirm the exact change and whether a rollback or config adjustment is needed. In the meantime, I'd recommend updating to the latest SDK version if you haven't already, as it includes updated backoff handling that should reduce retry bursts.

subject: Duplicate email alerts for same shipment event
body: We're seeing duplicate notification emails going out for the same shipment status change. This morning between 8:02 and 8:04 AM, three of our warehouse leads each got the same 'delivery delayed' alert twice for shipment ID SHP-88213. It's happening across almost every alert rule we have configured, not just one. This started sometime yesterday and is now flooding inboxes and causing confusion on the floor about which alerts are current.
answer: Thanks for flagging this, and sorry for the inbox noise it's causing on your team. We've seen a related issue where a retry in our notification dispatcher can double-fire on delivery-status webhooks, and we're treating this as an active incident. Can you confirm roughly how many alert rules are affected and send us one more duplicate example with timestamps so we can trace it in the queue while we push a fix?

subject: Request to scope API keys by webhook rate limit tier
body: As we roll out our new webhook integrations across regional teams, we'd like to propose a change to how API keys are managed. Right now every key we issue shares the same account-wide rate limit, which makes it hard to isolate a noisy integration from the rest. Could Northwind support per-key rate limit tiers, or at least a way to tag keys so we can throttle one webhook consumer without affecting others?
answer: This is great feedback, and you're not the first enterprise customer to ask for this. Per-key rate limit scoping isn't available today, but we can offer a workaround in the meantime: issuing separate keys per integration with distinct labels so at least usage is trackable per consumer in your API dashboard. I'll log this as a feature request against API Platform and follow up when there's movement on true per-key throttling.

subject: Slower Slack alert delivery after Jira integration added
body: Since we connected our Jira instance alongside our existing Slack integration a couple weeks ago, our Slack alerts for ticket updates seem to take longer to arrive, sometimes a minute or two instead of near-instant. It's not urgent since we're a small team, but we'd like to understand if the Jira and Salesforce connectors are competing for the same sync window, and whether reordering them would help.
answer: Thanks for the detail here, this helps a lot. Adding multiple connectors can queue events through the same integration worker, so it's likely the Jira sync is adding a short delay to Slack delivery rather than anything being broken. We'll take a look at your integration order and see if we can prioritize Slack alerts, and we'll let you know what we find within a few business days.

subject: Zapier integration completely stopped triggering Salesforce updates
body: Our Zapier connection between Northwind and Salesforce stopped working this morning. None of our Zaps have fired since around 6:30 AM, and we've got over 200 pending order updates that should have synced to Salesforce by now. This is affecting our entire logistics team's ability to track shipments, and we need this escalated immediately since finance reporting depends on this data being current.
answer: We understand how critical this is for your reporting and we're escalating this now. Our team is checking whether this is tied to a Zapier-side auth token expiration or an issue on our webhook delivery, and we'll update you within the hour with findings. In the meantime, could you confirm if you see any error codes in your Zap history so we can narrow this down faster?

subject: Login issues
body: So we've been using Northwind for a few months now across our energy trading desk and generally it's been fine, our team relies on SSO daily to get into dashboards and pull data first thing in the morning. But for the last THREE days people are getting kicked out constantly, sessions dying after like 5 minutes even with MFA passed, and I am absolutely done with this, if this isn't fixed today we are seriously looking at cancelling, this is affecting our ability to do our jobs and nobody has explained why.
answer: I'm sorry for the disruption this is causing your team, especially with how often it's happening. We're prioritizing this as a P2 investigation into the session timeout behavior with your SSO and MFA configuration right now. Can you tell us which identity provider you're using and whether this started right after any recent permissions or MFA policy change on your end, so we can pinpoint the cause as quickly as possible?

subject: Need Slack alert routing changed before next sprint
body: Our team has been using the Salesforce and Jira integrations for a while now, and generally things sync fine except for occasional lag we've learned to live with. The actual issue is with Slack: alerts for new Salesforce leads are now landing in the wrong channel entirely, going to #general instead of #sales-alerts, and this started right after we updated our Jira project mapping last week. This is blocking our sales team from seeing new lead notifications in real time, and we need the routing corrected before our sprint planning tomorrow.
answer: Thanks for the context, that timing lines up with a routing config change tied to project mappings. We're treating this as high priority since it's actively misdirecting your Salesforce lead alerts. Can you send us the exact Jira project key you updated last week? We'll check whether the Slack channel binding got reset during that mapping change and get the routing corrected before your sprint planning.

subject: Audit log missing entries for deactivated admin accounts
body: We're conducting a compliance review and noticed the audit log in Admin Console is missing entries for at least six admin account deactivations that occurred between March 3 and March 10. We rely on this log for our SOC 2 evidence collection, and the gaps mean we can't confirm when access was revoked for former employees. Our allowlist settings also don't seem to reflect changes made during that window. This needs investigation as soon as possible given our audit timeline.
answer: Thank you for reporting this, we recognize the urgency given your audit timeline and are escalating this as a P1 to our security and compliance team immediately. Can you provide the specific admin account identifiers or usernames affected so we can trace the deactivation events server-side and determine whether this is a logging gap or a display issue in the console? We'll keep you updated as we investigate.

subject: Frage
body:
Wir würden gerne Slack-Benachrichtigungen für neue Salesforce-Opportunities einrichten, aber beim Testen der Verbindung bekommen wir folgenden Fehler:

2024-05-14 09:12:03 ERROR integration.slack.webhook - Failed to deliver payload
HTTPStatusError: 403 Forbidden
  at SlackWebhookClient.send (webhook.py:142)
  at IntegrationSync.run (sync.py:88)
Retry attempt 3/3 failed, giving up

Können Sie uns sagen, ob das an fehlenden Berechtigungen in unserem Slack-Workspace liegt oder an der Konfiguration auf Ihrer Seite?
answer: Vielen Dank für die Log-Ausgabe, das hilft uns sehr. Der 403-Fehler deutet meist darauf hin, dass das verbundene Slack-App-Token nicht mehr die nötigen Scopes für den Ziel-Channel hat, oft nach einer Workspace-Berechtigungsänderung. Bitte prüfen Sie in Ihrem Slack-Adminbereich, ob die Northwind-App noch Zugriff auf den gewünschten Kanal hat, und teilen Sie uns mit, ob das Problem danach weiterhin besteht, damit wir die Konfiguration auf unserer Seite ebenfalls überprüfen können.

subject: Refund needed for duplicate charge on our invoice
body: I've been going through our billing history this week to reconcile our quarterly spend, and generally the invoices have matched our usage fine except for one thing I found today. Our invoice dated May 1st shows we were charged twice for the same billing cycle, once as our normal subscription charge and again as a separate credit card charge three days later for the identical amount. This has caused an overdraft situation for our team and we need this refunded urgently since it's actively affecting our account balance.
answer: I'm sorry to hear about the overdraft impact, we're treating this as urgent given the financial disruption. I can see this needs immediate review of the duplicate charge on your May 1st invoice, so I'm escalating this now to our billing team to verify the transaction and process a refund for the erroneous charge. We'll confirm the refund timeline with you within one business day.

subject: Shared dashboard export missing permissions for viewers
body: We recently shared one of our retail performance dashboards with a few external partners using view-only links, but when they try to export the chart data to CSV, they get an 'Access Denied' error even though the dashboard itself loads fine for them. This is blocking our partners from pulling the numbers they need for their own reporting. Could you check if export permissions are tied separately from view permissions on shared links?
answer: Thanks for the clear description, this is helpful. You're right that export permissions are currently governed separately from view access on shared dashboard links, which is likely why your partners can view but not export. We're looking into whether this should be adjustable per share link, and in the meantime we can walk you through granting export-specific access if you'd like to try that as a workaround.

subject: Alert routing sending duplicate notifications to on-call group
body:
We've noticed that our on-call escalation group for the Travel Ops workspace is getting duplicate copies of the same alert whenever a rule matches more than one routing tag. For example, alert ID ALR-88213 went out twice within 4 seconds this morning to the same email distribution list. This has been happening since we added a second routing tag last week.

Could you confirm whether alert routing is meant to dedupe across overlapping tags, or if there's a config step we're missing? A doc link on best practices for multi-tag routing would help too.
answer:
Thanks for flagging this - overlapping tags on the same alert rule can indeed cause duplicate dispatch if both tags map to the same channel without dedupe enabled. Please check Settings > Alerting > Routing Rules and confirm whether 'Dedupe across tags' is toggled on for that workspace; if it's off, enabling it should stop the duplicates immediately for new alerts.

I'm also attaching our routing best-practices guide covering multi-tag setups. Let us know if ALR-88213 and similar alerts continue after enabling dedupe and we'll dig into the routing logs directly.

subject: Transform step failing on every sync since this morning
body:
Our logistics data pipeline has been failing at the transform stage since around 6:40 AM. The connector pulls fine but every run since then errors out with 'transform timeout: row batch exceeded 30s processing window' on the shipments-hourly job. We've retried 5 times manually and it fails identically each time.

This is blocking downstream reports our dispatch team relies on every hour, so we need this looked at urgently. Job IDs are PL-4471, PL-4472, PL-4473 if that helps narrow it down.
answer: This is impacting your active pipeline so we're treating it as urgent. We can see elevated transform latency on the shared cluster serving your connector starting around 6:30 AM, which matches your timeline on PL-4471 through PL-4473 - we're actively investigating a resource contention issue there. In the meantime, could you try reducing the batch size on the shipments-hourly job to see if that gets runs through while we resolve the underlying capacity issue? We'll update you within the hour with root cause and an ETA.

subject: Question about allowlist and audit log settings in workspace
body: I'm reviewing our workspace configuration ahead of a security review and have a couple of questions about Admin Console settings. First, does adding an IP range to the allowlist affect performance for users connecting from outside that range, or are they just blocked outright? Second, is there a way to export the audit log for the last 90 days rather than viewing it only in the console?
answer: Good questions. Adding IP ranges to the allowlist only blocks or allows connections - it doesn't introduce any performance overhead for users inside the allowed range. For audit logs, you can export up to 90 days as a CSV from Admin Console > Audit Log > Export, or use the API endpoint if you'd like to automate the pull. Happy to walk through either in more detail if useful.

subject: Scheduled syncs randomly skipping runs - completely unreliable
body:
our schedueled syncs keep skipping runs with NO warning at all, we set it to run every 2 hours and its just... not running, sometimes it waits 6+ hours. this is the THIRD time this month were dealing with this and its messing up our inventory data badly, numbers dont match our warehouse system anymore.

we have 5 seats and cant afford to keep babysitting this, if this isnt fixed soon were going to have to look at other providers. job id is SY-1092 last skipped run was yesterday 3pm to 9pm gap
answer:
I'm sorry about the disruption this is causing your inventory data - a gap like that on SY-1092 is not expected behavior and I understand the frustration. I'm pulling the scheduler logs for that job now to see why the 2-hour cadence wasn't honored between 3pm and 9pm yesterday, and I'll also check whether this correlates with the earlier skipped runs this month.

I'll follow up today with findings and, if we confirm a scheduler bug, a fix timeline. In the meantime, if this is urgent for a specific report deadline let me know and I can trigger a manual sync for you right now.

subject: Adding trusted IP ranges to workspace allowlist
body: As part of a finance systems review, I'd like to restrict access to our Admin Console workspace to our office and VPN IP ranges only. Can you confirm the process for adding these to the allowlist, and whether this change would need to be escalated to a higher support tier given we're on the Starter plan?
answer: Adding IP ranges to your allowlist is available directly from Admin Console > Security > Allowlist for all plans including Starter, so no escalation is needed on our end. Simply add each CIDR range there and save - changes typically take effect within a few minutes. If you'd like, send over the ranges you plan to add and we can do a quick sanity check before you apply them.

subject: Dashboard charts not rendering for entire team
body:
Since about 9am today, charts across our main analytics dashboard are showing blank white boxes instead of rendering data, affecting all 25 users in our workspace. Exporting to PDF also fails with 'chart render error - no data context'. This is blocking our weekly reporting cycle which is due today.

We've tried refreshing, clearing cache, and switching browsers with no change. Dashboard ID is DB-3390, and this started right after we added a new shared filter yesterday afternoon.
answer: Thank you for the detailed report - a workspace-wide blank chart issue right after adding a shared filter strongly suggests the filter definition is breaking the chart's data context, and we're prioritizing this given your reporting deadline. Can you confirm the exact filter you added on DB-3390 so we can reproduce it? In the meantime, removing that shared filter should restore chart rendering for your team while we investigate the export error in parallel. We'll keep you updated as we dig into logs on our end.

subject: How do customers unsubscribe from our notification emails
body: We're getting complaints from a few retail store managers saying they can't find how to unsubscribe from certain alert emails, and some are getting the same alert twice from different rules. Can you point us to documentation on how end users manage their own notification preferences, and whether there's a way to dedupe alerts hitting the same recipient from multiple rules?
answer: There's an unsubscribe link at the bottom of every alert email that takes recipients to a preferences page where they can opt out of specific alert categories - I'll send over the doc that covers this in detail for your managers. For the duplicate issue, that's usually caused by a recipient matching more than one alerting rule; enabling 'Dedupe by recipient' in Settings > Alerting will consolidate those into a single email going forward.

subject: Upgrading plan but new features not showing up
body: We upgraded from Starter to Pro last week for our travel workspace, and the payment went through fine on our card ending in the usual digits, but we still don't see the advanced billing features listed as included in Pro. We waited a few days thinking it might just be a delay but nothing's changed.
answer: Thanks for reaching out - a successful payment should trigger the plan upgrade automatically, so this delay isn't expected. Can you confirm the workspace name and the date the payment was confirmed? I'll check our billing system to see if the upgrade is stuck in processing and get the Pro features unlocked for you as soon as possible.

subject: Duplicate alert emails going to finance team
body: Our finance team has been receiving duplicate copies of budget threshold alerts for the past two weeks - same alert, same timestamp, arriving twice about a minute apart. It's causing confusion since some people think there are two separate incidents. Is there a setting to prevent this, or a way to see if we have overlapping alert rules configured?
answer: This is usually caused by two alert rules both matching the same condition and each firing independently to the same recipients. Go to Settings > Alerting > Rules and filter by the budget threshold condition to check for overlaps - if you find two rules covering the same threshold, consolidating them into one should eliminate the duplicates. If you'd rather we check for you, share the rule names and we'll review the configuration directly.

subject: SDK throwing intermittent 429s despite low request volume
body:
We're seeing our Python SDK (v4.2.1) throw HTTP 429 rate limit errors intermittently even though our aggregate request volume is well under the documented tier limit for our Enterprise plan. This started after we rolled out a new webhook consumer service two days ago. We're logging this as a change request to consider separating webhook retry traffic into its own bucket for Enterprise accounts. In the meantime, adding jittered backoff in your webhook consumer should reduce clustering and should ease the 429 rate significantly - happy to review your retry logic if you'd like a second set of eyes.
