subject: Migrating off deprecated v1 API keys before June 30 cutoff
body:
We're using v1-format API keys for our billing integration and saw the deprecation notice that they'll stop working after June 30th. answer: Good timing on getting ahead of the June 30th cutoff. The new key format keeps the same X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers, so no changes needed there, but webhook signatures will use a new signing secret tied to the new key - you'll need to update your webhook verification logic to pull the new secret from the dashboard before switching over. We have a step-by-step migration guide for the Node SDK v4.1 that covers rotating keys with zero downtime by running both key formats in parallel briefly; I'll send the link and am also happy to set up a walkthrough call if you'd prefer.

We're aware this isn't ideal for quota-conscious accounts and have logged it as a feature request for selective restore. Happy to walk you through the temporary-location approach if useful.

body:
I'm trying to complete MFA enrollment for our finance team's Northwind accounts and three of us are stuck on a screen that says 'Enrollment failed, please contact your administrator' after scanning the QR code with an authenticator app. This started yesterday when we tried to enable mandatory MFA for our Delta Capital workspace, which has 19 seats total.

We can't log in at all now since MFA is required but won't complete. Two of the affected accounts belong to people who need to approve invoices today.
answer: I'm sorry for the login disruption, especially with time-sensitive approvals pending. This error typically occurs when the MFA policy was enabled before enrollment finished syncing across sessions, and I'm going to temporarily lift the mandatory MFA requirement for the affected accounts so your team can log in immediately while we investigate the enrollment failure. I'll follow up shortly with steps to re-enroll safely once we confirm the root cause.

subject: Need to update SSO role mapping for new department
body:
We're rolling out a new compliance team at Atlas Foods and need to map their SAML group to a custom role in Northwind that has read-only access to Identity and billing modules but not admin settings. Currently our SSO configuration only maps to the three default roles (Admin, Editor, Viewer), and none of them fit this use case.

Can you help us set up a custom role mapping, or point me to documentation on configuring attribute-based role assignment for our SSO setup?
answer: Thanks for the detailed requirements. Custom role mapping for SSO groups is supported on your plan, and it's configured through the Identity settings under SSO Attribute Mapping, where you can create a custom role and tie it to a specific SAML group attribute. I'll send over our step-by-step guide for creating restricted roles, and I'm happy to review your configuration once you've set it up to confirm the permissions match what you need.

subject: Transform jobs failing intermittently with connector timeout
body:
Since Monday, about 15% of our nightly transform jobs in Data Pipelines have been failing with a connector timeout error against our retail sales warehouse source. The failures aren't consistent, some nights it's 2 jobs, other nights 8, and they don't correlate with data volume that we can tell. Retrying manually usually succeeds on the second attempt.

This is affecting downstream reporting freshness for our 112 users who rely on next-day sales data. Could you check the connector logs for our Vertex Energy pipeline named 'retail-sales-nightly' around 2am UTC each night?
answer: Thank you for the detailed timeline and pipeline name, that will help us narrow this down quickly. Intermittent connector timeouts around a fixed time window often point to source-side throttling or a transient network issue between our connector and your warehouse, and I'm pulling the logs for 'retail-sales-nightly' now to check for patterns in the failed runs. I'll follow up with findings and, if needed, recommend a retry-backoff adjustment to reduce the downstream reporting delay.

subject: URGENT deprecated endpoint broke our production integration overnight
body:
You deprecated /v2/webhooks/register with ZERO warning that I saw and now every webhook registration call from our API integration returns 410 Gone. Our entire notification pipeline for Atlas Foods has been broken since last night and we are LOSING transaction alerts right now. I checked the changelog and found ONE line buried from three weeks ago, that is not acceptable notice for a breaking change.

We need this fixed or a working migration path IMMEDIATELY. This is a fintech product, missed alerts have real financial consequences. If this isn't resolved today we will be looking at other providers.
answer: I understand the severity here and I'm escalating this immediately given the financial impact. The v2 webhooks endpoint was deprecated in favor of /v3/webhooks/subscriptions, and I'm sending you the migration mapping right now along with a temporary workaround: we can re-enable a grace-period flag on your account within the hour to restore v2 functionality while your team migrates. I'll stay on this ticket personally until your webhook pipeline is confirmed working again.

subject: Connector auth failures breaking pipeline syncs since this morning
body: Our logistics data connector (warehouse-to-Northwind pipeline, ID pln-8823) started failing auth at 6:40am. Every sync attempt since then throws 'invalid_grant: token expired' even though we refreshed the credentials in the source system yesterday. We have 11 seats on this pipeline and all downstream dashboards are now showing stale data from yesterday. Latency on the last successful sync was already over 40 minutes before it broke entirely.
answer: Thanks for flagging this right away - I can see the failed auth attempts on pipeline pln-8823 starting at 6:40am on our end too. This looks like a token refresh mismatch after your credential rotation; I'm re-issuing the OAuth grant for the connector now and will confirm once a manual sync completes successfully. I'll follow up within the hour with root cause and steps to prevent this on future rotations.

subject: Getting duplicate alerts for every single event
body: Since yesterday afternoon we've been receiving two to three duplicate notifications for every alert we configured - shipment delay alerts, threshold breaches, all of it. We only have 3 seats so this is very noticeable and confusing our dispatch team who think something happened twice. Each duplicate has the same event ID and timestamp, just sent within a few seconds of each other via email.
answer: Sorry for the noise this is causing your dispatch team. Duplicate sends with identical event IDs point to a delivery retry issue on our notification queue - we're checking whether a recent webhook timeout setting is causing re-triggers. Can you confirm roughly how many duplicates you're seeing per hour so I can gauge scope while we investigate and push a fix?

subject: App crashes immediately on launch for field techs
body: We're getting reports from multiple field technicians that the mobile app crashes right at launch, before the login screen even loads. This started after the latest update went out and is happening on both iOS and Android devices. Offline mode users who had the app open before the update also report it crashing when they try to sync cached data. This is blocking our 160 field staff from clocking in and logging incidents on site.
answer: This is impacting your whole field team so we're treating it as urgent. We've had a couple of similar reports and are pulling crash logs now - could you send device models, OS versions, and the app build number from one affected phone? In the meantime, if any users still have the previous app version installed, ask them not to update until we confirm a fix.

subject: Need help configuring Okta app for SSO
body: We're setting up the Okta integration for our workspace and want to enable SSO before rolling out to our 6 seats. I've added the Northwind app from the Okta catalog but the SAML metadata URL field keeps rejecting the value we pulled from our Okta admin console - it says 'invalid issuer format'. We'd like this working today since we're onboarding two new team members tomorrow and want them to log in via SSO from day one.
answer: Happy to help get this sorted before tomorrow's onboarding. The issuer format error usually means the metadata URL includes a trailing slash or the wrong Okta org subdomain - can you paste the exact value you're entering (without any secrets) so I can check the format? I'll also send over our step-by-step Okta SAML setup guide in case it's faster to configure manually.

subject: issue
body: We noticed today that our audit log is missing entries for user deactivations that happened over the weekend - specifically three accounts we deactivated Saturday don't show up anywhere in the log even though the users are correctly showing as deactivated in the console. We rely on this log for our quarterly access review and this gap is a problem. Can you confirm if this is a display issue or if the events were never actually recorded?
answer: Thanks for catching this before your access review. We're checking whether this is a logging gap or a display filter issue on the audit log page - can you confirm the exact user IDs and deactivation timestamps for those three accounts? While we investigate, please hold off finalizing the quarterly review report so we can confirm whether the underlying event data exists.

subject: INVOICE
body: WE NEED A COPY OF OUR LAST TWO INVOICES FOR OUR ACCOUNTING TEAM BEFORE END OF MONTH. WE ALSO WANT TO KNOW IF WE CAN GET A REFUND FOR THE PARTIAL MONTH WHEN WE UPGRADED MID-CYCLE BACK IN FEBRUARY. PLEASE SEND DOCUMENTATION ON HOW PRORATION WORKS FOR OUR PLAN SO WE CAN EXPLAIN IT INTERNALLY.
answer: Happy to help with this. I'm attaching copies of your last two invoices now so your accounting team has them before month end. On the February upgrade, I'll check the proration calculation applied at the time and send you our documentation explaining how mid-cycle upgrades are billed, along with confirmation of whether a partial refund applies in your case.

subject: Audit log completely down and deactivations not being blocked
body: Our security team just discovered that the audit log has stopped recording any events as of approximately 2:15am today, and separately we found that deactivated users are still able to log in - two former employees accessed the system this morning after being deactivated last week. This is a compliance-critical failure for us given our fintech obligations and we need this resolved immediately. We manage 94 seats and need to know the scope of exposure right now.
answer: This has been escalated to our security and compliance team as our highest priority. We're investigating both issues in parallel: the audit log stoppage since 2:15am and the deactivation bypass allowing former employees to log in. We'll send an initial scope assessment within the hour, and in the meantime recommend you force-expire sessions for the two affected former employee accounts if you haven't already - we'll confirm system-side remediation as soon as we have it.

subject: Slack integration not escalating alerts to the right channel
body: We set up the Slack integration so that critical alerts escalate to our #incidents channel after 10 minutes if unacknowledged, but for the past week alerts are just staying in the original #alerts channel indefinitely. I checked the escalation rule configuration and it still shows the 10-minute threshold and correct destination channel, so I'm not sure why escalation isn't triggering.
answer: Thanks for the detailed description - that helps narrow it down. It sounds like the escalation timer may not be firing correctly rather than a channel routing issue. Can you share one specific alert ID that should have escalated so I can trace it through our system and see exactly where the escalation logic is stalling?

subject: Plan upgrade via API returning inconsistent results
body: I'm integrating the billing API to let our internal tool trigger plan upgrades automatically, but calls to the upgrade endpoint are behaving inconsistently. Sometimes the upgrade applies immediately and sometimes it returns a 200 response but the account plan doesn't change for several minutes, which is causing our tool to show incorrect plan status to users. We're also unclear on whether upgrade calls trigger an immediate prorated invoice or wait until next cycle - the docs don't specify this clearly.
answer: Thanks for the detailed report - the delay between the 200 response and the plan actually reflecting the change points to an async processing step on our end that isn't currently documented. I'll confirm with engineering whether there's a reliable way to poll for completion status, and I'll also get clarity on proration timing for upgrade calls so we can update the API docs. I'll follow up with both answers shortly.

subject: How do customers unsubscribe from notification emails
body: A few of our customers have asked how they can unsubscribe from certain notification emails without opting out of everything, and I want to make sure I'm pointing them to the right settings. Is there a way to unsubscribe from specific alert categories rather than all notifications at once? Also, could you point me to any documentation I can share with our customers directly, since a few have mentioned getting what looks like duplicate emails for the same alert too.
answer: Good question - yes, recipients can manage preferences per alert category from the unsubscribe link at the bottom of any notification email, rather than opting out entirely. I'll send over our notification preferences documentation that you can share directly with your customers. On the duplicate emails, could you have one affected customer forward an example so we can check whether it's a delivery issue on our side?

subject: Custom MFA enrolment flow via API
body: We're integrating Northwind Identity into our LMS and need to trigger MFA enrolment programmatically for new instructors instead of waiting for the first login prompt. I checked the /v2/users/{id}/mfa/enroll endpoint but it returns a 409 when the user hasn't logged in yet. Is there a supported way to pre-provision MFA enrolment state, or a webhook we can listen for once enrolment completes?
answer: Thanks for the detail — the 409 is expected because enrolment currently requires an initial session token before the enroll endpoint will accept a request. We do have a provisioning-side workaround: you can set force_mfa_enroll=true on user creation, which queues enrolment on first login and fires the user.mfa_enrolled webhook once complete. I'll also flag this as a feature request for pre-session enrolment since it sounds like a real gap for your onboarding flow.

subject: upgrade
body: Need to add 40 seats this week, how do we upgrade fastest?
answer: You can upgrade seats directly from the Billing tab under Plan & Seats — select the new seat count and it prorates automatically for the rest of your cycle. If you'd like, send over the exact count you need and I can apply it manually today so it's live before your deadline.

subject: Route pipeline failure alerts to Slack channel
body: We'd like our data pipeline failure notifications to post directly into a Slack channel instead of just email, similar to how our Jira integration creates tickets on errors. Right now I only see Slack listed under general notification settings, not tied to specific pipeline events. Is there a way to scope Slack alerts to just pipeline failures for our workspace, or is this something you're planning to add?
answer: Right now Slack notifications are workspace-wide rather than event-scoped, so pipeline failures would go to the same channel as everything else unless you create a separate Slack app integration filtered by event type on your end. I'll log this as a feature request for granular Slack routing by event category, since a few other customers have asked for the same thing with Jira-style filtering.

subject: Connector authentication failures across all pipelines - data not syncing
body: Since around 3:40am UTC today, every one of our data pipeline connectors (SAP, Salesforce, and our internal warehouse feed) is failing with 'authentication_error: token refresh rejected by provider'. No syncs have completed in over 5 hours and downstream retail inventory dashboards are now stale. This is affecting our entire 2107-seat org and we need this resolved immediately as store-level reporting is blocked.
answer: This is being treated as a P0 and we've escalated to the pipelines on-call team immediately. Initial checks show a certificate rotation issue on our OAuth token service that's rejecting refresh requests across connectors — we're rolling back the rotation now and will push a fix within the hour. I'll update you as soon as syncs resume and confirm no data was lost in the interim.

subject: MFA issue
body: Can't finish setup, blocked.
answer: Sorry you're stuck — to help narrow this down, could you tell me which MFA method you're enrolling (authenticator app, SMS, or hardware key) and what error or screen you're seeing when it stops? In the meantime, an admin can temporarily bypass MFA for your account from the Identity console under Users > Security if you need immediate access.

subject: Mapping SSO roles to custom permission groups
body: We're setting up SAML SSO and want incoming role claims from our IdP to map to our own custom permission groups rather than the default Northwind roles. Right now it looks like role mapping only supports the built-in Admin/Member/Viewer set. Is there a way to define custom mapping rules in the SSO configuration, or would we need to handle this via the provisioning API after login?
answer: Custom role mapping isn't available in the SSO config UI yet — currently incoming claims map only to the built-in roles. Your best path today is to use the provisioning API to reassign users to custom groups right after their first SSO login via the user.created webhook. I'll pass your use case to the identity team as feedback since custom claim mapping comes up fairly often.

subject: Dashboards timing out for entire finance team
body: Since yesterday afternoon, our monthly revenue dashboards are taking over 60 seconds to load or timing out entirely with a 'query execution exceeded limit' error. This is affecting everyone on the finance team, not just me, and we have a board reporting deadline tomorrow morning. The dashboards were fine last week and we haven't changed any filters or data sources.
answer: Thanks for flagging this urgently — we're seeing elevated query latency on the dashboard service starting yesterday and are actively investigating a likely indexing issue on larger date-range queries. Given your reporting deadline, I'm escalating this to P1 with our dashboards team now and will follow up within a couple of hours with either a fix or a workaround using a narrower date filter so you can pull the numbers you need in time.

subject: Linking Jira issues to Okta-authenticated API requests
body: We're building an integration that creates Jira tickets automatically when our Okta-authenticated API calls fail, and we want the Jira issue to include the Okta session ID for traceability. Is there a field in the Northwind Integrations API where we can pass custom metadata like this into the Jira ticket payload, or do we need to handle that mapping entirely on our side before calling the Jira connector?
answer: The Jira connector currently accepts a custom_fields object in the payload, so you can pass your Okta session ID there and map it to a Jira custom field of your choosing during setup. If you run into a 'field not recognized' error, that usually means the target field ID needs to be added to the connector's allowed fields list, which I can help configure if you send me the field key.

subject: Admin console down - cannot access workspace settings or deactivate users
body: Our entire admin console has been unreachable since about 20 minutes ago, returning 'service unavailable' when anyone with admin role tries to load workspace settings. We urgently need to deactivate several offboarded employee accounts today and can't reach any admin screens at all. With 282 seats and ongoing offboarding this is a critical outage for us.
answer: We're treating this as a P0 outage and have already identified elevated error rates on the admin console service starting around the same time you reported. Engineering is actively working the incident; in the meantime, if you have any pending deactivations, our support team can process them manually on your behalf if you send the list of user emails — otherwise we'll update you the moment console access is restored.

subject: Storage quota breach may indicate security issue - urgent review needed
body: Our storage usage jumped from roughly 40% to 98% of quota overnight without any corresponding upload activity from our teams, and we're now getting upload rejections across the board. Given the sudden spike with no legitimate cause we're identified, we're concerned this could be unauthorized data being written to our account and need this investigated as a possible security incident, not just a quota issue.
answer: Given the potential security implications, I'm escalating this immediately to our security and compliance team as a P0. We're pulling the storage write logs for your account now to identify the source of the spike and will confirm within the hour whether this is unauthorized activity or an internal process issue, along with a temporary quota increase so your teams aren't blocked while we investigate.

subject: Retention policy not deleting objects past 90-day mark
body:
I'm reviewing our storage buckets for Lumen Health's legal record retention and noticed that objects tagged with the 90-day retention policy from bucket lh-legal-archive are still present as of today, well past their expiry date (oldest is from January 3rd). We rely on this for compliance sign-off and now have roughly 4,200 objects that should have been purged automatically.

Can you check whether the retention job is actually running on our account? I also want to confirm whether this affects our quota calculations, since our usage dashboard shows we're at 94% of quota, which doesn't match what I'd expect if purging were working.
answer: Thanks for flagging this - a retention policy that silently stops purging is something we take seriously for compliance-tagged data. I've escalated this to our storage engineering team to check the retention job scheduler for the lh-legal-archive bucket and confirm whether the job has been failing or simply not triggering. In the meantime, please avoid manually deleting objects so we can preserve the evidence trail for the investigation, and I'll update you within one business day with findings on both the purge failure and the quota discrepancy.

subject: SDK throwing 'client.authenticate is not a function' after upgrade
body:
We upgraded the Northwind API SDK from 3.2.1 to 4.0.0 yesterday for our integration and now every call fails at startup with: TypeError: client.authenticate is not a function, at NorthwindClient.init (index.js:47). This is blocking our staging deploy and affecting all 10 devs on the team who pulled the new version.

Looking at the changelog I see authenticate was possibly renamed or deprecated in 4.0.0 but there's no migration note. Can you confirm the correct replacement method and whether this is a breaking change that should have been flagged more clearly?
answer: Sorry for the disruption this is causing your team. Yes, this is a confirmed breaking change in 4.0.0 - the authenticate() method was renamed to signIn() as part of the auth module refactor, and the migration guide unfortunately wasn't linked from the changelog, which we're correcting now. As a quick fix you can pin back to 3.2.1 while your team updates call sites to signIn(), and I'll send over the full migration notes shortly so you can complete the switch cleanly.

subject: Biometric login failing intermittently on Android app
body:
We're seeing reports from our travel agents in the field that Face ID and fingerprint login on the Delta Systems mobile app is failing intermittently, forcing a fallback to password entry. It seems to happen most often after the app has been backgrounded for more than a few minutes, and we've had around 30 tickets from users across our Android fleet this week.

This is becoming a friction point for adoption since biometric login was one of the features we pushed hardest to our field teams. Could someone look into whether this is a session token expiry issue interacting with the biometric unlock flow?
answer: Thanks for the detailed report - intermittent biometric failures after backgrounding usually point to a session token refresh timing issue, and your theory lines up with a pattern we've seen. I'm opening an investigation with our mobile team to trace the token lifecycle against the biometric unlock handler on Android specifically, and I'll ask if you can share Android OS versions and app build numbers from a few affected devices to help narrow it down. We'll keep you posted as we isolate the root cause given the impact on your field adoption.

subject: Request: bulk MFA enrolment options for new hires
body:
As we onboard new clinical staff at Orion Media, we're currently enrolling each user in MFA one at a time through the admin console, which is slow given our onboarding volume. I'd like to ask whether there's a bulk enrolment option or an API endpoint we could use to pre-provision MFA for groups of users during batch onboarding.

We use SSO for primary login already, so ideally MFA enrolment could be tied into that provisioning flow rather than being a separate manual step. Is this something on the roadmap or already possible with a setting we're missing?
answer: Good question, and this is a common ask from larger accounts like yours. There isn't a bulk MFA enrolment UI today, but our Identity API does support programmatic MFA factor registration that can be triggered as part of your SSO provisioning workflow - I can share the relevant endpoint documentation and a sample script to get you started. I'll also log this as a feature request for native bulk enrolment support in the admin console, since tying it directly to SSO provisioning is a reasonable enhancement to consider.

subject: Pipeline reporting revenue data hours late, finance close at risk
body:
Our nightly data pipeline that feeds the finance revenue dashboard for Summit Retail is arriving 4-6 hours late as of the last three nights (June 10-12). The pipeline job 'daily-revenue-sync' normally completes by 2am but hasn't finished until 8am each of those days, and this is delaying our monthly close process which needs the numbers ready by 9am.

We haven't changed our source data volume or schema recently. Can someone check if there's a bottleneck upstream, and let us know if this will resolve itself or needs manual intervention on our end?
answer: I understand the urgency given your close deadline, and I've escalated this to our data pipeline on-call team right now. Initial checks show elevated queue times on the ingestion layer that daily-revenue-sync depends on, which matches your timing - we're investigating whether this is a capacity issue or a stuck upstream job. I'll update you within the next couple of hours with either a fix timeline or a workaround so you can get the revenue numbers in time for close.

subject: Requesting adjustable SSO session timeout settings
body:
Our team at Granite Labs has noticed that SSO sessions are timing out after what seems like 30 minutes of inactivity, which is disrupting workflows for our legal staff who often step away between document reviews. We'd like to request the ability to configure a longer session timeout, ideally up to 2 hours, at the org level.

Is this something configurable today that we're missing in the admin console, or would this need to be a change on Northwind's side? We have 279 users affected by this and would appreciate a way to adjust it ourselves going forward.
answer: Thanks for the detailed feedback - session timeout duration is actually configurable at the org level under Identity settings > Session Policy, though the default of 30 minutes is quite conservative for workflows like yours. I'll walk you through adjusting it up to a 2-hour window, and I'd also like to note your feedback about the default being unclear in the console, since we've had similar requests and it may be worth revisiting the default guidance in our documentation.

subject: Push notifications not arriving on iOS since last app update
body:
Since rolling out the latest mobile app version to our Summit Travel field staff last week, push notifications for booking confirmations and itinerary changes are not arriving on iOS devices, though Android seems fine. We've confirmed device tokens are registered correctly in the admin console, and there's no error shown to users, notifications simply never appear.

We've had this reported by around 40 of our 237 seat holders so far, mostly iOS users on iOS 17. Can you check the push delivery logs on your end for our tenant to see if there's a delivery failure specific to iOS?
answer: Thanks for the clear breakdown, especially isolating this to iOS - that helps narrow the investigation. I'm pulling the push delivery logs for your tenant now to check for APNs certificate or payload errors that might be causing silent failures on iOS 17 devices specifically. I'll follow up shortly with what we find, and in the meantime if you can confirm the exact app version and a couple of affected device tokens, that will speed up tracing the delivery path.

subject: Need higher API rate limits for peak booking season
body:
As we scale our booking integration ahead of peak travel season, we're consistently hitting the current rate limit on the /bookings and /availability endpoints, seeing 429 responses during traffic spikes even though our actual usage pattern is legitimate customer demand, not abuse. This is affecting checkout completion for our 241 users relying on real-time availability data.

Could we discuss either a higher tier of rate limits for our account or a burst allowance mechanism? We're also open to SDK-level guidance on batching requests if that would help reduce our call volume without needing a limit increase.
answer: This is a great point to raise ahead of peak season, and I want to make sure you're not constrained by 429s during legitimate demand spikes. I'm looping in our platform team to review a burst allowance or tier increase for the /bookings and /availability endpoints on your account, and I'll also have someone from SDK support share batching and caching patterns that other travel customers have used to cut call volume. Let's get this resolved well before your peak period hits.

subject: How to export detailed audit logs for compliance review
body:
I'm setting up our compliance reporting for Atlas Retail and need to pull detailed audit logs from the Admin Console covering user deactivations, permission changes, and allowlist modifications over the past quarter. The console only shows the last 30 days of activity in the UI, and I need a way to export a longer history in a format our compliance team can review.

Is there an API endpoint or export tool for audit logs beyond the 30-day UI window? We also want to confirm whether allowlist changes are captured in the audit trail at all, since I don't see them listed in the current log entries.
answer: Thanks for reaching out - this is important to get right for your compliance review. There is an Audit Log export endpoint that supports querying beyond the 30-day UI window, and I'll send you the API reference along with a sample request for pulling deactivation and permission change events for the past quarter. On allowlist changes, I need to confirm with engineering whether those are currently captured in the audit trail, since you're right that they don't appear to be surfaced in the log entries today - I'll follow up as soon as I have an answer.

subject: Question about seat count discrepancy on latest invoice
body:
I'm reviewing our latest Northwind invoice for Atlas Retail and the seat count billed doesn't match what I see in our admin console. The invoice shows charges for 74 seats, but our admin console currently lists 68 active users, and we haven't added any seats in the past two billing cycles.

Could someone check where the extra 6 seats are coming from? If this is a billing error we'd like it corrected on this invoice or applied as a credit toward next month, since we need accurate seat figures for our internal budgeting.
answer: Thanks for catching this discrepancy and for the specific numbers - that makes it easy to investigate. I'm having our billing team cross-check the seat count on your account against the admin console's active user list to see whether this is a sync delay, deactivated-but-not-removed seats, or a billing system error. Once we identify the cause, we'll correct the current invoice or issue a credit toward next month as you requested, and I'll get back to you within a couple of business days.

subject: Dashboards taking 20+ seconds to load this week
body: Since Monday our regional consumption dashboard has been taking 20-30 seconds to render for our operations team, compared to the usual 2-3 seconds. It's the one we share weekly with our legal compliance group with the export-to-PDF chart included. Nothing has changed on our end that we know of - same filters, same date ranges. Can you check if something changed on the backend for slow queries?
answer: Thanks for flagging this - a slowdown of that magnitude on a previously fast dashboard is worth investigating right away. We're pulling query logs for your workspace now to see if this is tied to a specific chart type or the export function, and will check whether shared dashboard views are queuing differently than before. I'll follow up within the day with findings or a fix.

subject: Rate limit headers inconsistent with documented values
body: We're seeing our webhook calls to the API Platform get 429 responses well before hitting the limit stated in your docs. Our integration logs show we're throttled at around 480 requests/minute, but the documentation says the Pro tier allows 600/minute. I also noticed a deprecation notice mentioning v2 webhook endpoints will sunset soon but no firm date is given anywhere. Could someone confirm the actual current limit and the sunset timeline so I can plan our budget forecasting jobs accordingly?
answer: Good catch, and thanks for the detail. The 600/minute figure in the docs applies to the v3 endpoint; webhook calls routed through v2 are capped at 480/minute, which explains what you're seeing - we'll get that documentation page corrected. On the sunset date, I'll confirm the exact timeline with the API team and get back to you with a firm date rather than guessing.

subject: Requesting a fix or workaround for slow patient-metrics dashboard
body: Our clinical operations dashboard with the patient throughput charts has become nearly unusable over the past week, taking upwards of 15 seconds per chart to load. I've tried narrowing the date range and it helps only slightly. We rely on this being shared with two other departments daily, so the delay is becoming disruptive. Is there a caching option or chart optimization feature we could enable, or is this a bug on your end that needs fixing?
answer: Sorry for the disruption this is causing your team - a shared daily dashboard slowing down like this is exactly the kind of thing we want to get ahead of. We'll review the chart configuration and query load on your workspace to see if this is a caching gap or a bug tied to a recent update. In the meantime, splitting the largest chart into two smaller date-bounded views may reduce load time, and we'll report back once we've identified the root cause.

subject: Revenue chart showing blank data on shared dashboard
body: The revenue-by-department chart on our finance dashboard has been showing completely blank since yesterday, even though the underlying data source still has current records. Other charts on the same dashboard, like the expense breakdown, are rendering fine. We share this dashboard with two other finance leads and they're seeing the same blank chart. Nothing was changed in our chart configuration that I'm aware of.
answer: Thanks for the clear description - a single chart going blank while others on the same dashboard render fine usually points to either a filter mismatch or a broken data binding after a source update. We'll take a look at the chart's configuration and query on our end and let you know what we find. If you can share a screenshot of the chart settings panel, that would help speed up the diagnosis.

subject: Backup files disappearing before our retention period ends
body: We've set our backup retention to 90 days, but I just noticed that files uploaded in early January are already gone from Storage, well before the 90-day mark. This is a problem because we're required to keep training records on file for audits at our institution. Our quota usage also dropped suddenly around January 20th, which lines up with when the files vanished. Can someone check what happened and confirm whether these can be recovered?
answer: This is a serious issue and we're escalating it immediately given the compliance implications you've described. We're pulling the retention and quota logs for your account now to determine exactly when and why those January files were removed ahead of the configured 90-day window, and whether recovery is possible. We'll update you as soon as we have findings, and will treat data recovery as the priority if the files are still retrievable on our end.

subject: Need granular sharing permissions for dashboards by role
body: Right now when we share a dashboard, it's all-or-nothing access for anyone with the link, but we need to restrict certain chart exports to managers only while letting the wider team view charts without exporting. We manage freight scheduling dashboards that get shared across dispatch and finance, and export restrictions are becoming a compliance concern for us. Is there documentation on any role-based sharing options, or is this something we'd need as a feature request? Performance on the larger dashboards has also been sluggish when multiple users are viewing simultaneously, which compounds the concern.
answer: Role-based export restrictions aren't available in the current sharing model, which only supports link-level view access, so I understand why that's a concern for a compliance-sensitive workflow like yours. I'm logging this as a feature request and will escalate it to product for consideration, and I'll also loop in our performance team on the concurrent-viewer slowdown you mentioned since that's a separate but related issue worth investigating. I'll keep you updated on both threads.

subject: urgent
body: Users across our organization are being logged out of SSO sessions every 10-15 minutes since this morning, far shorter than our configured 8-hour session policy. This is affecting hundreds of employees trying to access financial systems and is causing major workflow disruption. MFA re-prompts are also firing on every re-login, which is compounding the problem. We need this resolved urgently as it's blocking core operations.
answer: This is being treated as a priority incident given the scale of impact you're describing. We're checking whether a recent session policy or identity provider configuration change is causing the timeout to override your 8-hour setting, and looking into why MFA is re-triggering on each login rather than respecting the existing session. We'll have an engineer actively working this and will update you with findings within the hour.

subject: audit log empty
body: Audit log shows nothing since 6am today, all blank.
answer: Thanks for the alert - an audit log going completely blank is something we're treating as urgent. We're checking the logging pipeline for your workspace now to see if this is a display issue or an actual gap in data capture, and whether any settings or account changes around that time triggered it. We'll follow up shortly with what we find.

subject: SCIM provisioning not creating accounts for new hires
body: We set up SCIM provisioning through our identity provider a couple weeks ago, and it worked initially, but for the last three new hires added to our directory group, no accounts were created in Northwind. I checked the provisioning logs on our IdP side and the push shows as successful with a 200 response, but the users never appear in our admin console. Is there a delay on your end, or should I be looking at a permissions issue with the SCIM token?
answer: Thanks for the detail, including the 200 response on the IdP side - that's helpful for narrowing this down. A successful push with no resulting account on our end usually points to either an expired SCIM token scope or a mapping issue on specific attributes for those users, so we'll check the provisioning logs on our side for the last three attempts and compare timestamps. We'll follow up with what we find and whether the SCIM token needs to be reissued with updated permissions.

subject: Incorrect seat count on latest invoice
body: Our most recent invoice bills us for 1,824 seats, but our admin console shows we're currently at 1,790 active users after offboarding a batch of contractors last month. This discrepancy is causing an issue for our internal finance reconciliation process. Could someone review the invoice and confirm whether we're due a credit or refund for the difference, and clarify how seat counts are calculated relative to the billing cycle cutoff?
answer: Thanks for flagging the discrepancy and for the specific numbers - that helps us investigate quickly. Seat counts are typically calculated as of the billing cycle cutoff date rather than current-day usage, so the offboarded contractors may not have been reflected yet at invoice generation, but we'll verify this against your account history rather than assume. We'll review the billing cycle dates against your offboarding timeline and follow up with either an explanation of the timing or a credit adjustment if an error is confirmed.

subject: Plan upgrade charged wrong amount and duplicated invoice
body:
We upgraded Orion Energy from Starter to Pro on March 3rd to cover our 23 seats, but the invoice generated (INV-88213) charged us for 46 seats at the Pro rate. A second invoice (INV-88214) was also generated the same day for the same period. Our card was charged twice, totaling $4,180 instead of the expected $2,090.

We need this reversed immediately since it's affecting our month-end close. Can you confirm which invoice is correct and process a refund for the duplicate charge?
answer: Thank you for flagging this, and I'm sorry for the billing confusion during your upgrade. This looks like a known issue where the seat-count multiplier doubled during the plan migration, causing the duplicate invoice. I'm escalating this to our billing engineering team right now and will personally confirm which invoice (INV-88213 or INV-88214) is the correct one, along with initiating a refund for the duplicate charge within 24 hours. I'll follow up shortly with confirmation and a corrected invoice.

subject: Request to add audit log entry for allowlist changes
body:
While reviewing our workspace settings for a compliance audit, our security team noticed that changes to the IP allowlist under Admin Console aren't being recorded in the audit log. We can see login events and role changes logged, but not when someone adds or removes an entry from the allowlist.

This isn't blocking us right now, but for our SOC 2 review next quarter we'd like to know if this is a known gap or if there's a setting we need to enable to capture these events.
answer: Thanks for bringing this to our attention. You're correct that allowlist modifications are not currently captured in the audit log by default; this is a known limitation rather than a configuration issue on your end. I've logged a feature request with our product team to add this event type, and I'll update this ticket once we have a timeline. In the meantime, if you need an interim workaround for your audit, we can provide a manual export of allowlist change history from our backend on request.

subject: Adjusting sync schedule for retail transaction connector
body:
We're using the retail transactions connector in Data Pipelines and currently have it set to sync every 6 hours. We'd like to change this to every 30 minutes to reduce latency for our fraud detection reports, but I don't see a way to set a custom interval below 1 hour in the connector settings UI.

Is there a way to configure sub-hourly syncs, either through the UI or via the API? We're on connector version 3.2 for the Atlas Retail workspace.
answer: Good question, and thanks for the connector version detail. Sub-hourly sync intervals aren't exposed in the UI yet, but you can configure this through our Pipelines API by setting the `sync_interval_seconds` field on the connector config endpoint, with a minimum supported value of 900 seconds (15 minutes). I'll send over a sample request body for your connector type, and let us know if you'd like help testing it in a staging pipeline first.

subject: Slack alerts from Salesforce integration stopped firing
body:
Since yesterday around 2pm, our Salesforce-to-Slack integration has stopped sending alerts to the #sales-alerts channel. We rely on this for new opportunity notifications, and our sales team hasn't received any pings since then even though new records are being created in Salesforce.

I checked the integration status page in Admin Console and it shows 'Connected' with no errors, but nothing is coming through. We have 91 users depending on this, so we'd appreciate a quick look.
answer: Thanks for the detailed report. We're seeing a pattern of Slack webhook delivery failures affecting several Salesforce integrations since yesterday afternoon, likely tied to a token refresh issue on our end. I'm escalating this to our integrations team now as a priority fix and will update you as soon as we have alerts flowing again. In the meantime, could you confirm the integration ID from your Admin Console so we can verify the fix on your specific instance once deployed?

subject: Getting duplicate email alerts for same event
body:
Our team has been getting two identical email notifications for every storage quota warning over the past week. For example, on Tuesday we received two emails at 9:14am and 9:16am both flagging that our storage usage hit 80%. This is happening for every alert type, not just storage.

It's not urgent since the alerts are still useful, but it's cluttering inboxes for our 16 users and a few people have asked if there's a way to reduce this to one email per event.
answer: Thanks for the clear example with timestamps, that's helpful. Duplicate notifications like this are usually caused by overlapping alert rules or a subscription being set up twice under different conditions. Could you check under Notifications settings whether the same alert type appears under both an individual and a team-level rule? If you'd rather not dig through it, send me a screenshot of your current alert rules and I'll identify the duplicate for you.

subject: App crashes after enabling biometric login on Android
body:
After updating to the latest Northwind mobile app version (4.8.2) and enabling Face unlock in settings, the app crashes immediately on launch every time. This started happening this morning on two of our four company devices, both running Android 13. Uninstalling and reinstalling didn't fix it.

We rely on the mobile app for field data entry, so having 2 out of 4 devices down is a real problem for us today. Is this a known issue with the latest update?
answer: Sorry for the disruption this is causing your field team. We've had a couple of similar reports of crashes tied to biometric login on Android 13 after the 4.8.2 update, and our mobile team is actively investigating a fix. As a temporary workaround, please try disabling Face unlock under device Settings > Security before reopening the app, which should restore normal launch behavior. I'll keep this ticket open and update you as soon as a patched version is available.

subject: Request for webhook retry documentation and SDK examples
body:
We're building an internal billing reconciliation tool using the API Platform webhooks for invoice.paid and invoice.failed events. I can see webhooks are firing, but I can't find documentation on retry behavior when our endpoint returns a 500 error, or how many attempts are made before Northwind gives up.

Could you point me to documentation on retry policy, and also let me know if there are SDK examples for handling webhook signature verification in Node.js? We're an 18-seat team so building this ourselves rather than paying for a dedicated integration.
answer: Happy to help point you in the right direction. Our webhook retry policy performs up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff over roughly 24 hours before marking a delivery as failed, and you can see delivery attempt history under Webhooks > Delivery Logs in the API Platform console. For Node.js signature verification, our official SDK includes a `verifyWebhookSignature` helper; I'll send over a link to the relevant docs page and a small code sample in a follow-up message.

subject: Feature request: offline biometric login for mobile app
body:
Several of our field finance staff use the Northwind mobile app in warehouses with poor connectivity, and biometric login currently seems to require a network check every time, which fails when offline and forces a fallback to password entry. With 250 seats and a lot of mobile-first users, this is becoming a recurring complaint.

Is there a roadmap item for allowing biometric login to work fully offline once a device has been previously authenticated? Happy to provide more detail on our usage pattern if useful.
answer: Thanks for the detailed context on your field team's usage pattern, this is genuinely useful for prioritization. Offline biometric login isn't currently supported since we require a token refresh check on each login, but I've logged this as a feature request with our mobile product team, referencing your account and the connectivity constraints you described. I'll update this ticket if it gets added to a near-term roadmap, and please let us know if you'd like to be included in beta testing when available.

subject: Deactivated user still appearing in allowlist and active sessions
body:
I deactivated a former contractor's account in Admin Console yesterday at around 4pm (user ID usr_3f82a1), but their IP is still showing as active in our allowlist settings, and the audit log shows a successful login from their account at 8:03am today, after deactivation. This is a real security concern for us since they shouldn't have any access anymore.

Can someone confirm whether deactivation is actually revoking session tokens, or if there's a delay/bug causing this?
answer: Thank you for reporting this promptly, this is exactly the kind of thing we take seriously. We're escalating this now to confirm whether user usr_3f82a1's active session token was properly revoked at deactivation time, and we're checking for a possible bug in the session invalidation flow. As an immediate precaution, please rotate any API keys or shared credentials this user may have had access to while we investigate, and I'll update you within the next few hours with findings.

subject: PDF export failing for large dashboards, all users affected
body:
Since this morning, exporting any dashboard to PDF results in either a blank page or the export hanging indefinitely at 'Generating PDF...' for several minutes before timing out. This is happening across our entire Harbor Analytics workspace, affecting all 3651 seats, and we use PDF export daily for board reporting that's due this afternoon.

We've tried exports on three different dashboards, all with the same result. Nothing has changed on our end recently; this started without any configuration changes we're aware of.
answer: I understand the urgency given your reporting deadline this afternoon, and I'm treating this as a top priority. We're seeing reports of PDF export timeouts starting this morning that appear linked to a rendering service issue on our end, and our engineering team is actively investigating with the goal of restoring full functionality as quickly as possible. I'll update you within the hour with progress, and in the meantime I'd recommend using the CSV or PNG export options as an interim workaround for your board materials.

subject: Unsubscribed users still getting duplicate alert emails
body:
I'm the IT admin for Pioneer Analytics and we're seeing a problem with the Notifications unsubscribe flow. Several users unsubscribed from the weekly digest alerts on March 3rd, but they're still getting the emails - and in some cases getting the same email twice within a few minutes. I've confirmed in the admin panel that their subscription status shows as 'opted out' for at least 14 accounts.

This is causing complaints and making us look bad internally. Can you check if there's a delay or caching issue in the unsubscribe pipeline?
answer: Thanks for the detailed report and the specific date - that helps us narrow this down quickly. This looks like it could be related to a known caching delay in our unsubscribe processor where the opt-out flag doesn't propagate to the send queue in time, causing duplicate sends for users who unsubscribe close to a scheduled digest run. I'm escalating this to our alerting team to check the queue logs for March 3rd and will confirm once we've identified the root cause.

subject: URGENT UPLOAD FAILURES RETENTION POLICY BROKEN
body:
WE ARE INTEGRATING THE STORAGE API AND GETTING FAILURES WHEN TRYING TO SET A CUSTOM RETENTION PERIOD ON UPLOADED BACKUP FILES. HERE IS THE ERROR WE GET REPEATEDLY SINCE THIS MORNING:

PUT /v2/storage/buckets/vertex-backups-prod/objects/backup-2024-05-14.tar.gz
HTTP 422 UNPROCESSABLE ENTITY
{"error":"retention_policy_invalid","message":"retention_days must be between 30 and 3650"}
request_id: req_8834ncx91

WE ARE SENDING retention_days=7 BECAUSE OUR COMPLIANCE TEAM ONLY NEEDS SHORT TERM STORAGE FOR THESE FILES. IS THERE NO WAY TO SET SHORTER RETENTION OR DO WE NEED TO CHANGE OUR BACKUP SCHEDULE ENTIRELY. WE HAVE 293 SEATS DEPENDING ON THIS PIPELINE AND UPLOADS ARE STUCK.
answer: Thanks for sending the request ID and error payload, that confirms what's happening - our current minimum enforced retention is 30 days, so any request below that will return the 422 you're seeing. There's no way to set a shorter value on this plan tier, so you'll need to adjust retention_days to at least 30 in your upload calls to unblock the pipeline right away. I'll also flag this to our docs team since the minimum isn't clearly called out in the current API reference for the retention_days field.

subject: Request to change offline login behavior causing crash on launch
body:
I'm a data analyst at Harbor Systems and I've noticed our field teams' mobile app crashes on launch whenever the device was offline during the last session. It seems to happen specifically when the app tries to refresh the cached login token without connectivity - the app just closes immediately after the splash screen, no error message shown.

Can we request a change so the app falls back to the last valid session instead of forcing a token refresh on launch? This is affecting warehouse staff who often work in areas with poor connectivity, roughly 30-40 crash reports a week from our side.
answer: Thank you for the clear description - this matches a behavior we've seen where the offline token refresh attempt on launch can crash instead of gracefully falling back to the cached session. I'm logging this as a change request for our mobile team to review the fallback logic, and in the meantime I'd recommend having affected users do a full sign-out and sign-in once they have connectivity to reset the cached token state, which should reduce crash frequency until the fix ships.

subject: Seat count discrepancy on our invoice
body:
I manage IT for Granite Academy and I'm reviewing our latest invoice, which shows billing for 22 seats, but we only have 16 active user accounts provisioned in the admin console. We removed 6 users back in January when a training cohort ended, and I expected the seat count to adjust automatically.

Could someone review our account and correct the seat count going forward? We're on the Starter plan and this overcharge is a concern for a small academy like ours - I'd like this resolved before the next billing cycle.
answer: Thank you for flagging this and for the specific numbers - I've pulled up your account and can see the deprovisioned users from January are still showing as billable seats due to a sync delay between the admin console and billing system. I'm correcting the seat count to 16 now and will apply a credit for the overcharged difference on your next invoice; please allow a couple of billing cycles for the automatic sync to catch future changes, though I'd also recommend confirming removals reflect correctly next time you offboard users.

subject: Storage uploads failing intermittently since yesterday
body:
Our team at Summit Health has been unable to complete file uploads to Storage since yesterday afternoon. Several uploads over 500MB are failing partway through with a generic 'upload interrupted' message in the dashboard, and retrying doesn't help. We checked our quota usage and we're at about 78% of our allocated storage, so it doesn't seem like a quota limit issue.

This is affecting our media asset backups and we have a retention deadline approaching for compliance archiving. Can someone check if there's a service issue on your end?
answer: Thanks for the quota check, that rules out one common cause quickly. We're seeing some elevated error rates on large multipart uploads over 400MB in your region starting yesterday, and our infrastructure team is actively investigating a possible issue with the upload gateway timing out on larger files. I'll keep this ticket open and update you as soon as we have a fix or a workaround for uploads over that size threshold.

subject: Questions about API key rotation and rate limits
body:
I'm the operations lead at Cobalt Robotics and we're setting up our first integration with the API Platform. I noticed a deprecation notice mentioning our current API key format will stop working in a future release, but I couldn't find clear guidance on how to rotate keys without breaking our existing webhook subscriptions.

Also, could you clarify the rate limit for our Starter plan - the docs mention 100 requests/minute but I want to confirm this applies per key or per account before we finalize our SDK setup.
answer: Good questions, and happy to clarify both. Key rotation can be done from the Admin Console under API Keys - generating a new key doesn't automatically invalidate existing webhook subscriptions, so you can create the new key, update your integration to use it, and then revoke the old one once confirmed working, with no downtime. On rate limits, the 100 requests/minute cap on the Starter plan applies per account rather than per key, so rotating keys won't give you additional headroom - let us know if you're anticipating needing higher limits as you scale.

subject: Dashboards laden sehr langsam bei großen Datensätzen
body:
Ich bin Support-Ingenieur bei Pioneer Capital und seit letzter Woche laden unsere Dashboards extrem langsam, besonders die mit mehreren Diagrammen zu Lieferzeiten. Ein Dashboard mit 6 Charts braucht teilweise über 20 Sekunden zum Laden, früher waren es 2-3 Sekunden.

Auch der Export als PDF bricht bei einem unserer größeren Dashboards mit einem Timeout-Fehler ab. Können Sie prüfen, ob es aktuell Performance-Probleme bei den Dashboard-Diensten gibt? Wir haben 292 Nutzer, die täglich auf diese Dashboards zugreifen.
answer: Vielen Dank für die genaue Beschreibung. Wir sehen aktuell erhöhte Ladezeiten bei Dashboards mit mehreren Diagrammen, die auf große Datensätze zugreifen, und unser Team untersucht bereits eine mögliche Verzögerung im Chart-Rendering-Dienst. Für den PDF-Export-Timeout empfehle ich vorübergehend, das Dashboard in kleinere Ansichten aufzuteilen, bis wir die Ursache der Verzögerung gefunden haben - wir melden uns mit einem Update, sobald es Neuigkeiten gibt.

subject: Incorrect line items on last two invoices
body:
I'm integrating with the Billing API for North Freight and noticed our last two monthly invoices, dated April 1 and May 1, both include a line item for 'API overage - 15,000 requests' even though our usage dashboard shows we stayed under our included quota both months. The overage charge added about $180 extra each time.

We're not disputing legitimate overages, but the numbers don't match what the /usage endpoint returns for our account. Can someone check where the discrepancy is coming from before we get billed again next cycle?
answer: Thank you for pointing out the specific invoice dates and the mismatch with the usage endpoint - that's a helpful lead. We're looking into whether the overage calculation is pulling from a different usage aggregation window than what's exposed via the /usage endpoint, which could explain the discrepancy. I'll get billing to reconcile both April and May charges against your actual usage logs and issue a correction or credit if the overage was applied incorrectly.

subject: Urgent: need to restrict workspace settings access immediately
body:
I'm a product manager at Apex Works and we just discovered that several non-admin users have been able to modify workspace-level settings, including the IP allowlist, without any audit log entry being created. This is a serious compliance gap for us given we're mid-audit this quarter with only 18 seats total but very sensitive manufacturing data.

We need to restrict settings changes to admin roles only and confirm audit logging is capturing all changes going forward. This needs to be addressed today if possible given the ongoing audit.
answer: This is a priority for us given the audit timeline - thank you for flagging it right away. I'm escalating this to our security team now to review the permission scoping on workspace settings and confirm why changes to the IP allowlist aren't generating audit log entries; this shouldn't be happening on any plan tier. In the meantime, I'd recommend temporarily restricting settings-edit roles via the Admin Console's role management page while we investigate, and I'll follow up within the next few hours with findings.

subject: Deactivated users still showing as active via API
body:
I'm integrating our HR system with the Admin Console API at Ember Foods and running into an issue where calling the deactivate endpoint for a user returns a 200 success response, but the user still shows status 'active' when I query GET /v1/users/{id} right after, and they can still log in. This is happening consistently, tested with three different user IDs over the past two days.

Our audit log also shows no deactivation event recorded for these attempts, which is a bigger concern given we rely on this for offboarding compliance. Can you look into why the state isn't updating?
answer: Thanks for the reproducible detail with the three user IDs - that will help us trace this quickly. A 200 response with no state change and a missing audit log entry suggests the deactivation might be silently failing at a downstream step after the initial API acknowledgment, rather than an issue with your request format. I'm escalating this to our access management team as a priority given the offboarding compliance impact, and will update you as soon as we identify why the status update and audit logging aren't completing.

subject: Late-arriving data breaking downstream syncs on retail pipeline
body: We're integrating with the Data Pipelines API for our retail feed (pipeline id vtx-retail-04) and since Nov 6 we're seeing records arrive 3-6 hours after their event timestamp. Our downstream sync job assumes a 30 minute watermark and is now dropping roughly 8-12% of records per run because they land after the window closes. This is affecting inventory counts across 40+ stores. Can you confirm if there's a connector delay upstream or if we need to widen our watermark immediately?
answer: Thanks for the detailed report. We can see elevated ingestion lag on vtx-retail-04 starting around 06:00 UTC on Nov 6, correlating with a backlog on the upstream connector queue. We're escalating this to our pipelines engineering team now and will push a fix to drain the backlog; in the meantime we recommend temporarily widening your watermark to 6 hours to avoid further drops. We'll update this ticket within the hour with progress.

subject: Offline mode capabilities for field staff
body: Our field coordinators often work in areas with no signal and we'd like to understand what the Mobile App supports for offline use. Can staff view previously loaded student rosters and attendance records without connectivity, and will any changes they make sync automatically once they're back online? We couldn't find this documented anywhere and want to plan a pilot with about 15 users next semester.
answer: Good question, and thanks for planning ahead. Currently the Mobile App caches the last-loaded rosters and attendance views for offline viewing, but edits made offline are not yet queued for auto-sync - that's on our roadmap but not available today. I'll send over our current documentation on cached data limits and flag your use case to our product team as a vote for offline write support.

subject: App crashes immediately on launch for one staff member
body: One of our staff members reports that the Mobile App crashes within a second of opening it on her device, right after the splash screen. She's on an Android tablet and reinstalling didn't help. Everyone else on our team of 243 can open the app fine. She needs it mainly for push notifications about court filing deadlines, so this is disrupting her workflow.
answer: Sorry to hear about the crash. Could you have her check her Android version and app build number in Settings, and send us the device model? Since this seems isolated to one user, it may be a corrupted local cache - please have her try clearing app storage/data (not just reinstalling) and let us know if the crash persists. We'll also check our crash logs on our end using her account email once you confirm it.

subject: Migrating webhook endpoints ahead of deprecation notice
body: I got the email about the v1 webhook signing scheme being deprecated on Jan 15 and want to make sure we migrate correctly before then. We only have a couple of webhook subscriptions set up for order status updates. Is there a guide for updating to the new signing method, and do we need to regenerate our webhook secret or update the SDK version we're using?
answer: Thanks for getting ahead of this. Yes, you'll need to update to SDK v3.2+ which supports the new HMAC-SHA256 signing scheme, and regenerate your webhook secret from the API dashboard under Webhooks > Signing Keys. I'm attaching our migration guide which walks through updating the signature verification code - it's a small change, should take under an hour given you only have two subscriptions.

subject: Repeated transform failures in patient intake pipeline
body: We're getting intermittent transform step failures in our patient intake pipeline (pipeline id apx-intake-02), roughly 5-10 failures per day over the past week. The error shown is 'transform_error: null value in column patient_dob violates not-null constraint' but the source data does have DOB populated for those records when we check manually. Can someone help us understand why the transform step is seeing nulls?
answer: Thanks for flagging this - it sounds like a timing issue between your connector sync and transform execution rather than actual missing data. We've seen this happen when the transform runs before a batch fully commits upstream. Can you confirm your connector's sync frequency and whether these failures cluster around specific sync windows? In the meantime, adding a short delay buffer between sync completion and transform trigger should reduce these failures while we investigate the root cause.

subject: Connector down, need urgent help
body: We've been running our logistics pipelines smoothly for months, syncing shipment and warehouse data across three regional connectors without much issue. Over the past quarter we've scaled up considerably and added a couple of new data sources to keep pace with our growth, so our pipeline team has been fairly heads-down. This morning, though, our primary warehouse connector (pwh-conn-11) started failing every sync attempt with 'authentication failed: token expired or revoked' and none of our shipment data has updated since 4am. This is blocking our entire ops dashboard for the day and we have no visibility into current shipment status across 101 warehouse users.
answer: This is now our top priority - we're treating this as a P1 outage. We're checking the OAuth token refresh service for pwh-conn-11 right now since 'token expired or revoked' typically indicates a refresh token failure on our end. We'll have an update within 30 minutes and will manually re-authenticate the connector if needed to restore your sync immediately.

subject: Request to adjust late-arrival handling for legal document pipeline
body: We've noticed our document ingestion pipeline (pipeline id sml-docs-07) regularly receives records timestamped up to 2 hours after our current 45-minute late-arrival window closes, causing them to be excluded from daily reconciliation reports. Rather than continuing to manually re-run reports, we'd like to request either a configurable late-arrival window per pipeline or an option to auto-reprocess excluded records. Could you let us know what's currently possible?
answer: Thanks for the clear writeup. Today the late-arrival window is configurable per pipeline, so we can extend sml-docs-07's window to 3 hours on request - just confirm and we'll apply it. Auto-reprocessing of previously excluded records isn't available yet, but I've logged it as a feature request with your use case attached, since it's a reasonable ask we've heard from a few other Data Pipelines customers.

subject: How to route alerts to different email groups by severity
body: We want to set up alert routing so that critical system alerts go to our IT lead's inbox while lower-priority notifications go to a general staff distribution list. Right now everything seems to go to one email address regardless of severity. Is there a way to configure this in the Notifications settings, and if so could you point me to instructions?
answer: Yes, this is supported - under Notifications > Alert Rules you can create separate routing rules based on severity level and assign different recipient email groups to each. I'll send you a short walkthrough doc; it should take just a few minutes to set up two rules, one for critical and one for general, given your current single-recipient setup.

subject: Getting duplicate alert emails for same transaction flags
body: Since last week we've started receiving duplicate email alerts for the same flagged transaction events - sometimes 2, sometimes 3 copies of the identical alert within a few minutes. This is happening across most of our fraud alert rules and is causing confusion among our 56 users who monitor these. It started around Nov 3 without any change on our end to alert configuration that we're aware of.
answer: Thanks for the report, and apologies for the noise this is causing. We've seen similar duplicate-delivery reports tied to a recent change in our alert dispatch retry logic that started around that date - we're investigating whether retries are firing even on successful delivery. We'll update you as soon as we have a fix, and in the meantime you can add a dedup key check on your side if you're processing these alerts programmatically.

subject: Speicherkontingent überschritten - Uploads schlagen fehl
body: Seit heute Morgen können unsere Mitarbeiter keine neuen Dateien mehr in Storage hochladen. Die Fehlermeldung lautet 'quota exceeded: storage limit reached for workspace'. Wir haben letzte Woche unser Kontingent geprüft und lagen deutlich darunter, daher vermuten wir einen Fehler bei der Berechnung. Für uns betrifft das 206 Nutzer im Retail-Bereich, die aktuell keine Belege und Rechnungen mehr hochladen können. Bitte dringend prüfen, das blockiert unseren Tagesbetrieb.
answer: Vielen Dank für die Meldung, wir stufen dies als P1 ein und prüfen sofort. Es könnte sein, dass ein fehlerhafter Backup-Snapshot-Prozess fälschlicherweise Speicherplatz belegt hat, ohne dass er in Ihrer regulären Nutzungsübersicht sichtbar war - wir untersuchen das gerade auf Workspace-Ebene. Wir melden uns innerhalb der nächsten 30 Minuten mit einem Update und werden bei Bestätigung das Kontingent manuell korrigieren, damit Uploads sofort wieder funktionieren.

subject: SCIM deactivation delay for offboarded users
body: We rolled out SCIM provisioning for our identity and SSO setup about two weeks ago. When we deactivate a user in our identity provider, Northwind still shows them as active for up to 48 hours afterward. On Oct 3 we deactivated 3 accounts on the travel ops team, but they could still sign in via SSO until Oct 5. It's only a handful of accounts so far, but I wanted to flag it before we scale provisioning to the rest of the org.

subject: Mobile app crashes on reconnect after offline sync

subject: Plan upgrade failed

subject: Node SDK throwing deprecation errors after v3.2 update

We haven't changed our integration code, just bumped the dependency. Is this expected with 3.2, and is there a migration guide for the rate limit changes?
answer: Thanks for flagging this - v3.2 did change the rate limit client internals, and the deprecation warning is expected, but the unexpected 429s at low volume are not. We'll check whether the new rateLimits.fetch() path has a bug in how it tracks your quota. Could you share your API key prefix and a couple of request IDs from the failed calls so we can trace them server-side?

subject: Frage zur Pagination bei API-Anfragen
body: Wir nutzen die API Platform, um Mandantendaten für unsere Kanzlei abzurufen. Können Sie uns bestätigen, ob offset weiterhin funktioniert oder ob wir zwingend auf page_token umstellen müssen? Wir wollen unsere Integration nicht auf Basis einer veralteten Methode aufbauen.

Wir empfehlen ausdrücklich die Umstellung auf page_token, da nur dieser Ansatz mit größeren Datensätzen und zukünftigen Rate-Limit-Anpassungen kompatibel bleibt. Gerne verweisen wir Sie auch auf unser Migrations-Guide im Entwicklerportal, falls Sie Unterstützung bei der Umstellung benötigen.

subject: PDF export cutting off charts on multi-panel dashboards

I'm escalating this to our dashboards team given your deadline, and in the meantime you can work around it by exporting in landscape mode or splitting the dashboard into two exports of 3 panels each.

subject: Best practices for pagination with high request volume
body: Our operations team pulls production line data through the API Platform on a rolling basis, and we're hitting rate limit errors (429s) when paginating through large result sets quickly. We use cursor-based pagination already, but we fetch pages back-to-back with minimal delay. Is there a recommended pacing strategy, and does the SDK have built-in retry/backoff logic we should be using instead of our custom loop?
answer: Good question, and this is a common pattern we can help optimize. Our official SDK does include built-in exponential backoff and automatic retry handling for 429 responses, so switching to it instead of your custom pagination loop should resolve most of the throttling. If you're not using the SDK, I'd recommend adding a small delay (100-200ms) between page requests and respecting the Retry-After header we return on rate-limited responses.

subject: Speicherkontingent erreicht - Uploads blockiert

subject: Seat count on invoice doesn't match active users

subject: Deprecated endpoint still required by our SDK integration

subject: How to rotate API keys without breaking active integrations
