In the meantime I'm reviewing our SSO logs for Harbor Health's tenant to pinpoint the exact validation error, and I'll have an update for you within the hour.

subject: Best practices for managing IP allowlist entries
body: I'm setting up our IP allowlist in Admin Console for the first time and want to make sure I do it correctly before we roll it out to our 9 users. Is there documentation on the recommended format for CIDR ranges, and does adding a new range immediately deactivate sessions for users outside it, or only affect new login attempts? Also wondering if changes to the allowlist show up in the audit log automatically.
answer: Thanks for checking before rolling this out. Our documentation on IP allowlist configuration covers accepted CIDR formats and is linked in the Admin Console help panel under Security Settings. To answer your questions: adding a new range only affects new login attempts, it won't force-deactivate existing active sessions, and yes, every allowlist change is automatically logged in the audit log with the admin's identity and timestamp. Let us know if you'd like feedback on your planned ranges before you apply them.

subject: Slow performance after IP allowlist update
body: We updated our IP allowlist in Admin Console yesterday to add three new office locations. Since then, login times have noticeably increased for our 250 users, sometimes taking 15-20 seconds instead of the usual 2-3 seconds. We also noticed a few deactivation events in the audit log that we didn't initiate around the same time. Nothing else changed on our end. Can you check if the allowlist update is causing this slowdown?
answer: Thank you for flagging both issues together. We're also pulling the audit log entries around those unexpected deactivation events to determine whether they're related to the same update or a separate cause, and will share findings within the next few hours.

subject: SCIM provisioning failing to deactivate users
body: We're seeing an issue where our SCIM integration is successfully creating new users but failing to deactivate them when removed from our identity provider. Over the past week we've counted at least 47 users who were removed from our IdP group but still show as active in Northwind with SSO login still working. Our SCIM logs show a 200 response for the DELETE calls but the accounts remain in an active state on your side. This is a permissions and security concern given our size at 3249 seats. Can you check why deactivation isn't propagating despite the successful API responses?

A 200 response on DELETE with no actual state change points to an issue in our SCIM deprovisioning handler not committing the status update correctly - we're pulling logs for your tenant now to trace those 47 accounts specifically. Given the security implications of stale active sessions, we're treating this with priority and will provide both a fix timeline and a list of affected accounts you may want to manually deactivate in the meantime.

subject: Late-arriving data breaking downstream reports
body: We've noticed that data from our Salesforce connector has been arriving 4-6 hours later than usual for the past three days, consistently landing after our nightly aggregation jobs run at 2am. This means our morning dashboards are showing incomplete numbers for our retail clients, and we've had two client escalations already. I'll have an update within a few hours on whether this is a temporary API quota issue or something requiring a pipeline schedule adjustment, and we'll also look at whether we can push a manual backfill once resolved.

subject: Users being logged out every 15 minutes
body: Since this week, our finance team members are being logged out of Northwind approximately every 15 minutes, requiring them to re-authenticate through SSO each time. In parallel we're reviewing your tenant's auth logs to pinpoint the exact timeout value being applied.

subject: URGENT: Deactivated users still have active access

subject: urgent
body:

subject: Scheduled sync delays on media connector

subject: MFA enrollment failing for new users
body:

subject: Scheduled sync failing intermittently for inventory connector
body:
Our nightly inventory sync job (scheduled for 1:30 AM) has failed on 3 of the last 5 runs, each time with a partial data load rather than a clean failure. answer:

We'll compare source and destination record counts for the last 5 runs and get back to you with findings.

In the meantime, if this is time-sensitive for reporting, we'd recommend manually re-triggering the sync and validating record counts before relying on last night's data.

subject: Data arriving hours after scheduled sync window
body:
I'm integrating with the Data Pipelines API for our education platform and noticed that data from our source system is consistently arriving 3-4 hours after the scheduled sync completes. The sync job itself reports success at the expected time, but when I query the destination via the API right after, recent records are missing until much later.

This is blocking a downstream reporting feature we're trying to ship this week - our small team really needs either a fix or clear guidance on how to detect when data has actually landed versus when the job status says complete.
answer:
Thanks for the clear writeup - late-arriving data behind a successful sync status is a known gap for a few source connectors, and we want to get you unblocked quickly since this is holding up your release. As an immediate workaround, you can poll the /sync-runs/{id}/watermark endpoint, which reflects actual data landing time rather than job completion, and use that as your trigger for downstream processing.

We're also flagging this to engineering as a priority fix so the job status more accurately reflects data availability, and will update you here once that's addressed.

subject: Requesting change to connector authentication method
body:
We'd like to switch our retail data connector from the current API key authentication to OAuth2, since our security team is phasing out static keys company-wide by end of quarter. Before we make the change, I want to understand whether switching auth methods will interrupt our existing scheduled syncs or require reconfiguring any of our 14 active pipelines.

Could someone walk us through the migration steps and any downtime we should plan for?
answer:
Good timing on this - OAuth2 migration is straightforward and we can help minimize disruption to your 14 pipelines. The switch itself doesn't require deleting existing pipeline configs; you'll re-authenticate the connector under the new OAuth2 flow and existing schedules and mappings carry over automatically, though we do recommend pausing scheduled runs for about 15-20 minutes during the cutover to avoid any auth errors mid-sync.

I'll send over our step-by-step migration guide for this connector type, and we're happy to hop on a call if you'd like us to walk through it live before your end-of-quarter deadline.

subject: Mobile app crashes immediately on launch
body:

We're pulling crash logs from our monitoring for your account now and will follow up shortly with next steps.

subject: Duplicate alerts being sent to wrong distribution list
body:
Our manufacturing team set up alert routing rules last week so that critical inventory alerts go to the operations distribution list and billing alerts go to finance. Since then, we're seeing every alert - both types - duplicated and sent to both lists, which is generating a lot of noise and confusion among our 16 users.

answer: Thanks for the clear description and for double-checking your rule config first. This sounds like it could be a rule evaluation order issue where both rules are matching before the category filter is applied - can you send us the rule IDs or a screenshot of the routing configuration so we can trace exactly which conditions are firing? In the meantime, adding an explicit exclusion condition to each rule (category != other type) should stop the duplicates while we investigate the underlying matching logic.

subject: Upload failures hitting storage quota unexpectedly
body:
We've started seeing upload failures across our travel document storage over the past two days, with the error 'quota exceeded' even though our dashboard shows we're only at 78% of our allocated storage. This is affecting multiple teams trying to upload itinerary and booking documents, and it's starting to back up our processing queue.

Can someone check whether there's a discrepancy between our reported usage and actual quota enforcement? We also want to confirm our retention and backup policies aren't being affected by this.
answer:
Thanks for flagging this with the usage discrepancy details - that's a useful clue, as 'quota exceeded' errors while showing 78% usage often point to a stale usage calculation rather than an actual capacity issue, and we're escalating this to our storage team to verify the enforcement numbers against your account. To confirm, your retention and backup policies are not affected by this issue and no data has been lost; this is isolated to new upload validation.

We'll update you as soon as we've confirmed the root cause, and if this continues to block uploads today, let us know and we can look at a temporary quota override while we investigate.

subject: Webhook rate limits and deprecation timeline for v1 endpoints
body:
We're planning a larger rollout of webhook-based order notifications across our retail integrations and want to understand two things before scaling up: first, what the current rate limit is for webhook delivery attempts per endpoint per minute, since we're expecting a spike during peak hours; second, we noticed a deprecation notice on the v1 webhook payload format and want to confirm the timeline for migrating to v2 before we build against it.

We have 268 users depending on this integration working reliably, so we'd like to plan the migration properly rather than react to a breaking change later.
answer: Thanks for planning ahead on this - it'll make the transition much smoother. Current webhook delivery rate limits are 600 requests per minute per endpoint with burst allowance up to 1000 for short spikes, and we recommend building in exponential backoff for 429 responses if you expect sustained peak traffic. On the v1 to v2 payload migration, v1 is scheduled for sunset in 90 days; the v2 format adds a few new required fields but is otherwise backward compatible, and we can share the migration guide and a sandbox endpoint so your team can test against v2 before switching production traffic over.

subject: Upgrade from Starter to Pro failed mid-checkout, double billed
body: We called /v1/billing/plan this morning around 9:40am ET to move Willow Capital from Starter to Pro. subject: URGENT CARD DECLINES BLOCKING RETAIL CHECKOUT RENEWALS

subject: Push notifications not delivered after app comes back online
body: I'm integrating push through the Northwind Mobile SDK for our iOS app and noticed that when a user's device is offline for more than a few minutes and then reconnects, queued push notifications never arrive, they just silently drop. I've reproduced this on iOS 17.4 with SDK version 4.2.1, tokens look valid in the device logs. Is there a retry window or delivery TTL we need to configure on our end?
answer: Thanks for the detailed repro steps, this matches a known limitation where push payloads sent while a device is offline expire after our default 5 minute TTL rather than queuing indefinitely. You can extend this by setting the ttl parameter on the send call, up to 24 hours, which should cover most reconnect scenarios. I'll also flag your case to our mobile team as a vote for making the default TTL configurable at the app level.

subject: Need itemized invoice reflecting recent seat count change
body: We added two seats to our Cobalt Systems Starter plan last week, bringing us to 5, but our latest invoice still shows the old seat count and total. I need an itemized breakdown showing the seat change with prorated charges so I can pass it to our finance team before month end.

subject: Connector token expiring every night on ERP source

subject: Scheduled sync deleted 3 days of records instead of updating

subject: Data issues in weekly report

subject: Grace period needed for MFA enrollment on new hires
body: We're rolling out enforced MFA across our Pro workspace and it's working well for existing staff, but new hires are getting locked out immediately since MFA enrollment is required before first login with no grace window. I'll log this as a feature request for a configurable enrollment grace window and update you here if it moves into our roadmap.

subject: Storage quota alert conflicting with retention backup policy

In the meantime I'll confirm the exact date your current allocation is projected to be exhausted so we can get ahead of any risk to scheduled backups.

subject: Connector authentication failing for energy usage pipeline
body: Since this morning our Data Pipelines connector to the utility billing source (connector ID PL-4471) has been failing with 'OAuth token refresh rejected: invalid_grant'. This has stopped syncing usage data for all 200 seats since 06:12 UTC today. We rely on this feed for month-end close and finance reporting is due in two days, so this is urgent. subject: Slack alert delays from Integrations hub

subject: Need SAML attribute mapping support for provisioning

answer: Thanks for the report - this looks like a quota caching issue rather than an actual limit breach, since your usage is well under the allocated cap. I've triggered a manual quota recalculation for your tenant, which should resolve the failed uploads within the next 15-20 minutes. If uploads still fail after that, please send me one of the file names and the exact timestamp so we can trace it further.

subject: Salesforce sync duplicating contact records

It's not frequent - maybe 1 in 50 records - but it's creating some noise in our CRM. Is this a known limitation of the sync matching logic, or is there a config option to match on a different unique field like external ID instead of email?

We do support matching on external ID as an alternative key; I can walk you through switching that in your integration settings, or if you'd prefer, I can make the change on our end for your Salesforce connector.

subject: URGENT AUDIT LOG ISSUE

subject: MFA setup question

subject: SAML role mapping not assigning correct group after SSO login

answer: Sorry for the disruption this is causing across your team. subject: How to restrict workspace settings changes to admins only
body: I'm reviewing our Admin Console setup for Ember Labs and want to lock down who can edit workspace-level settings like the domain allowlist and deactivation policies. Right now it looks like any user with the Manager role can modify these, which isn't ideal for our audit requirements. Is there a way to scope this down to just Owner/Admin roles, and would that change be reflected in the audit log?
answer: Good question - you can restrict workspace settings edits to Owner and Admin roles under Admin Console > Roles > Permission Scopes, by unchecking the 'Workspace Settings' toggle for the Manager role. Any changes made through that panel are automatically captured in the audit log with timestamp and actor, so you'll have a clean record for compliance reviews.

subject: Jira integration losing linked issues after sync
body: We connected our Harbor Labs workspace to Jira last week and set up the link so that support tickets auto-create Jira issues in our ENG project. We're going to check the integration logs for your workspace around Tuesday's failures and will also verify the API scopes on the connected Jira app - we'll follow up shortly with findings.

subject: Question about sharing dashboards with view-only access
body: I'd like to share our quarterly spend dashboard with two external auditors but only give them view access, not edit rights. When I tried the Share option it only lets me add people who already have a Northwind account under our domain. Is there a way to generate a public or view-only link instead, since we're on the Starter plan with just 7 seats and don't want to add extra logins for a one-time review?
answer: On the Starter plan, dashboard sharing is currently limited to workspace members, so external guest links aren't available yet - that feature is part of our Pro tier. As a workaround, you could export the dashboard as a PDF or CSV snapshot for the auditors, which keeps the data static and avoids needing to add new accounts.

subject: Shared dashboard shows stale data for recipient
body: I shared our 'Device Uptime' dashboard with a colleague on the ops team here at Pioneer Robotics, and when they open it the charts show data from three days ago even though my own view is fully current. We both have the same refresh interval set. Refreshing the page on their end doesn't help, and they've tried two different browsers. This is a Pro workspace so caching settings should be standard across users.
answer: Thanks for the report - stale data on shared views is usually caused by a cached snapshot being served instead of a live query, which can happen when the share link was generated before the last data refresh. Can you try re-sharing the dashboard fresh (rather than reusing the existing link) and let us know if your colleague then sees current data? If not, we'll dig into the caching layer for that specific dashboard.

subject: Need to add one-click unsubscribe to all outgoing alert emails
body: As part of a compliance review, we need every alert email sent from our Apex Retail workspace to include a one-click unsubscribe option, not just the weekly digest. Right now our escalation and threshold alerts don't have any unsubscribe link at all, which our legal team flagged as a problem. Can you confirm how to enable this across all notification types, and whether it applies retroactively to templates we've already customized?
answer: This is a valid concern and we can help get this configured. One-click unsubscribe can be enabled workspace-wide under Notifications > Email Settings > Compliance Footer, and it applies to all alert types including escalation and threshold alerts going forward. For templates you've already customized, you'll need to re-save them once the footer setting is toggled on so the link gets injected - we can walk you through that if needed.

subject: MFA enrolment failing via API for new SSO users - blocking rollout
answer: This has been escalated given the impact on your rollout timeline. We're investigating now and will update you within the hour with either a fix or a workaround, such as adding a short delay or a status check call before enrollment.

subject: Best practice for cursor-based pagination on large result sets
body: We're planning a change to how our integration pulls data from the API Platform and want to switch from offset pagination to cursor-based pagination for our /reports endpoint, since our result sets are growing past 50,000 rows and we're hitting rate limits on repeated offset queries. Is cursor pagination supported for that endpoint, and if so, is there guidance on how the cursor token expires or interacts with our webhook-triggered polling jobs?
answer: Cursor-based pagination is supported on /reports via the 'next_cursor' field returned in each response, which you can pass as a query parameter to fetch the next page without re-scanning offsets. Cursor tokens are valid for 24 hours and are safe to use alongside webhook-triggered polling, though we'd recommend starting a fresh cursor if a job resumes after that window to avoid a 410 expired_cursor error.

subject: Duplicate charges on last 3 invoices - need refund

subject: Wiederholte Transform-Fehler bei Rechtsdaten-Connector

subject: How to route alerts to different email groups by severity
body:
I'm setting up notification routing for Lumen Retail and want low-severity alerts to go to our general support inbox while critical ones go straight to on-call engineers. Right now everything seems to land in one shared address and we're getting duplicate emails for the same alert too.

Is there a way to configure routing rules based on severity tags, and separately, any idea why alerts might be duplicating? We're only on 12 seats so keeping noise down matters a lot for us.
answer:
Good question - you can set this up under Notification Rules by creating separate routing conditions filtered on the severity tag, then pointing each rule to a different destination address or webhook. I'll include a quick walkthrough link in a follow-up so you can map critical vs low-severity alerts to the right inboxes.

On the duplicates, that's often caused by two overlapping rules matching the same alert - I'd suggest checking if you have a catch-all rule alongside your severity-specific ones, as that combination is the usual culprit.

subject: Connector auth token expiring mid-pipeline, breaking scheduled runs
body:
Our Salesforce connector in the retail-sales pipeline keeps losing its auth token partway through the nightly run. We saw it fail twice this week, on the 12th and the 14th, both around the 40-minute mark with a token expired error even though we refreshed credentials just three days ago.

Is there a way to enable automatic token refresh mid-run instead of only at job start? Also curious if there's a way to get latency metrics per connector step so we can pinpoint where time is going before the token times out.
answer:
Thanks for the detailed timestamps - that helps narrow this down. It sounds like your OAuth token's TTL is shorter than your run duration, and currently our connector only refreshes at job start rather than mid-run, which explains the failures around the 40-minute mark.

I'm logging a feature request for mid-run token refresh, and in the meantime I'd recommend splitting the nightly job into shorter batches as a workaround. I'll also point our product team to your request for per-connector latency metrics, as that would help diagnose exactly this kind of issue going forward.

subject: SAML login redirect loop for finance team members

subject: App crashes immediately after login on iPad

subject: Jira integration not linking issues correctly

subject: How to handle recurring transform failures in shipment pipeline

subject: Questions on plan upgrade process and seat billing
body: We're planning to upgrade from our current plan tier to accommodate additional seats for a new regional office opening next quarter, and I want to understand how the upgrade affects our existing invoice cycle. If you downgrade later, any unused prepaid amount for the current cycle is credited rather than refunded directly. subject: Upcoming API deprecations affecting our integration
