subject: Bulk sharing permissions for dashboard folders
body:
We manage about 40 dashboards across three teams at Vertex Analytics and currently have to share each one individually with view or edit access. It would save a lot of time if we could set sharing permissions at the folder level and have them inherit down to new dashboards added later.

Also, exporting a shared dashboard with 15+ widgets sometimes takes 20-30 seconds before the PDF generates - not urgent, just noting it in case it's related to permission checks running per widget.
answer:
Thanks for the detailed feedback! Folder-level sharing inheritance isn't available today, but I've added your use case to our product team's backlog for the Dashboards sharing feature - it's a common ask so it's good to have another data point.

On the export delay, that's likely tied to rendering time for widget-heavy dashboards rather than permission checks, but I'll flag it to engineering to see if there's room to optimize for large exports.

subject: okta setup broken
body:
trying to connect okta app to salesforce sync, getting this:

ERROR: SAML assertion validation failed
code: OKTA_SAML_INVALID_AUDIENCE
expected: https://app.northwind.io/sso/quillenergy
got: https://app.northwind.io/sso/quill-energy

need this fixed to launch by friday
answer:
Thanks for the detailed error - this is a mismatch between the Audience URI configured in your Okta app and the SSO endpoint registered on our side (quillenergy vs quill-energy). I can update our end to match whichever slug your Okta admin has set, or you can adjust the Audience URI field in Okta to use quillenergy exactly.

Let me know which you'd prefer and I'll turn it around today so you're not blocked for Friday's launch.

subject: Occasional delays in scheduled sync completion
body:
I've noticed our nightly sync job for the manufacturing inventory connector has been finishing later than usual over the past week - typically it completes by 2am but on Oct 14, 16, and 18 it didn't finish until closer to 4:30am. No errors in the sync logs, just longer runtimes.

We're not seeing any downstream data issues, just wanted to flag the latency pattern in case it's a sign of something on the pipeline side. Happy to share sync IDs if useful.
answer:
Thanks for the heads-up and the specific dates - that's helpful. We've seen some increased load on a few connector pools recently which could explain the extended runtimes without triggering errors. If you can send over the sync IDs for those three runs, I'll have our pipelines team check resource allocation for your connector specifically.

We'll also keep monitoring on our end and let you know if we identify a root cause or need to adjust your sync window.

subject: PDF export cuts off chart legends
body:
When I export any dashboard to PDF, the chart legends on the right side get cut off if there are more than 5 series in a line chart. This happens consistently on our production dashboard and it's making the exports unusable for the reports we send to our leadership team each week.

I've tried both the 'Fit to page' and 'Actual size' export options and the legend is cropped either way. We're a small team of 4 so this is blocking our weekly reporting workflow.
answer:
Sorry for the trouble this is causing your weekly reports. This sounds like a rendering issue where the legend width isn't accounted for in the PDF layout when there are many series - I've reproduced a similar cropping issue on our end and I'm escalating it to engineering as a bug.

As a workaround in the meantime, try switching the legend position to 'bottom' instead of 'right' in the chart settings before exporting - that's avoided the cropping in our tests. I'll update you here as soon as we have a fix timeline.

subject: Increased transform failures on large pipeline jobs
body:
Over the past two weeks we've seen a noticeable uptick in transform step failures on our larger data pipeline jobs, particularly ones processing over 5 million rows. The failures don't show a consistent error message - sometimes it's a timeout, other times the job just shows 'failed' with no detail in the pipeline logs.

Given we're running this across 2,202 seats and multiple business units, we'd like to request better visibility into transform-level failure reasons, ideally with row-level error context, and would appreciate any guidance on whether there are known limits for row counts per transform step we should be designing around.
answer:
Thanks for the detailed report - given the scale you're operating at, I want to make sure we get this right. I'm looping in our pipelines engineering team to look at the failure patterns on large jobs and will ask them to check if there's a resource ceiling being hit around the 5 million row mark for transform steps.

On visibility, more granular transform failure logging is something we've heard requested before; I'll file this as a formal feature request tied to your account and keep you posted on both the investigation and any roadmap movement.

subject: Card declined error when testing billing API
body:
I'm integrating the Billing API for Summit Freight and testing card charge scenarios in our sandbox environment. When I simulate a failed card charge using test card 4000000000000002, the API returns a 402 but the response body doesn't include a decline_code field, just a generic message 'Your card was declined.'

We need the decline_code to build proper error handling for our checkout flow before going live. Is this expected behavior in sandbox, or is there a way to get more detailed decline reasons in the response?
answer:
Good catch - in sandbox mode, decline_code is currently only populated for a subset of test card numbers that simulate specific failure types (insufficient_funds, expired_card, etc). The generic decline card you're using returns a minimal response by design, which doesn't reflect what you'd see in production.

I'll send over our list of test cards mapped to specific decline codes so you can test each error handling path properly. If you still see missing decline_code fields in production once you go live, let us know right away and we'll dig deeper.

subject: Dashboard shared externally without permission review
body:
We discovered that one of our analysts shared a financial dashboard containing client transaction data with an external email address using the 'Anyone with link' sharing option, bypassing our internal approval workflow. This happened on Oct 22 and the link remained active for about 6 hours before we caught it and revoked access.

Given we're in fintech and this involves sensitive financial data, we need to understand what sharing controls exist to prevent 'Anyone with link' from being available at all for dashboards tagged as containing sensitive data, and whether there's an audit trail showing who accessed the link during that window.
answer:
Thank you for reporting this promptly - given the sensitivity involved, I'm escalating this to our security and compliance team right away. We can pull the access logs for that specific link to show any views or downloads during the 6-hour window it was active, and I'll have that report to you within one business day.

On prevention, we do support restricting 'Anyone with link' sharing at the workspace level for Pro plans, which would disable that option entirely for all dashboards. I'll walk you through enabling that restriction and also check if we can apply tag-based sharing rules for sensitive dashboards specifically.

subject: Dashboards extremely slow to load for all users
body:
Starting about an hour ago, every dashboard in our workspace is taking 30-60 seconds just to load initial widgets, and several users are seeing partial renders where charts never finish loading at all. This is affecting all 22 of our seats and we use these dashboards for live customer support metrics, so our team is currently working blind.

Nothing changed on our end - no new dashboards created, no sharing changes. This started suddenly around 2:15pm today. We need this resolved urgently since it's blocking our support operations.
answer:
I'm sorry for the disruption - this is impacting your live operations so we're treating it as urgent. We're checking for any ongoing performance incidents on the Dashboards service around the 2:15pm start time you mentioned and will confirm within the next 15 minutes whether this is a broader issue or isolated to your workspace.

In the meantime, could you let us know if this affects all dashboards equally or specific ones with heavier data loads? We'll keep you updated here continuously until this is resolved.

subject: IP allowlist not deactivating old entries
body: I'm the finance manager at Cobalt Freight and I manage our Admin Console settings for compliance reasons. We removed an old office IP range (203.0.113.0/24) from the allowlist on Monday, but the audit log still shows access attempts from that range being permitted on Wednesday. Can someone confirm whether deactivated allowlist entries actually take effect, or if there's a caching delay we should know about? We need this documented for our healthcare compliance review.
